## Q-28 + Q-10 — value, representation, presentation; composable display filters — 2026-10-07

### Q-28 — what "the same value" means on the Decimal128 tier

1. **2026-08-20 · Decimal128 end to end (#153): CREATES the question.** `==` became `Decimal128.Equals` (NaN one value, `-0 == 0`, quantum ignored) while display and `.string` kept every quantum and zero sign, so `==`-equal numbers became distinguishable by observers.
2. **2026-09-23 · D1 (5d6d60b) and the Lean law: STATES it too strongly.** AGENTS' D1 wording promised a permutation-invariant "complete resulting binding"; `repeated_name_complete_binding_is_permutation_invariant` holds only up to `BEq` (exact on `Int`). C# kept the first equally `==` contribution (`P(1.5, 1.50)` is `'1.5'`, `P(1.50, 1.5)` is `'1.50'`).
3. **2026-09-29 · Q-05 (repeated names are constraints, not merges): NARROWS it.** The value channel's representative stays open; the `P(1.5, A)` no-splicing residue is recorded under PAT-09.
4. **2026-10-02 · Model C (NEED-04): NARROWS it further.** One richest compatible complete contribution is retained, so `P(1.5, A)` and `P(A, 1.5)` both give `'1.50'`; only the tie among equally rich contributions remains.
5. **2026-10-06/07 · investigation (`../q28-q10-numeric-identity-display/`): RECOMMENDS N-F** (1,290 probe variants × six routes; the alternatives N-C, N-E and N-O change 376–627 outcomes; N-F changes none).
6. **2026-10-07 · owner decision Q-28: ADOPTS N-F.** "The same value" is `==` for every consumer; representation is data; a repeated name keeps the first equally rich contribution, representation included; literal patterns match by `==`. Implemented as tests, C#-only spec cases and documentation only (no production code change); X-28 and X-12 resolved; new rule VAL-11.

**Surviving semantics (owner follow-up, 2026-10-07).** Three layers — VALUE (`==`), REPRESENTATION (data, preserved, observed by `.string`), PRESENTATION (inert rendering). Permuting all contributions of one repeated name preserves satisfiability. On success it preserves the bound VALUE up to `==`, callable identity and channel availability; among equally rich compatible contributions, the first in written traversal order supplies the retained representation. Failure reporting follows ordinary binding order (NEED-04, PAT-10, Q-27): when different incompatibilities coexist, permutation may change the error category, blamed contribution, payload, message or span, although every permutation still fails.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "the complete binding is permutation-invariant" (exactly, at representation level); "`==`-equal Decimal128 values are different values"; a canonical or synthesized representative; a representation-sensitive second equality for patterns, `distinct` or repeated names.

The source filter is read only by `KatLangEngine`, after successful output, by the ordinary cached value read in the same run, whatever the host filter is; it can trace, draw, spend steps, be cancelled or fail; the rendering step is inert.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "a declared `DisplayDecimals` overrides the host default" (D-H); "the host setting overrides the program"; "display precision is host configuration only" (D-O); "the engine/evaluator divergence has disappeared"; "a stricter host filter skips or excuses the source read"; "`null` / off means zero decimals".

## Q-16 — owner-local Grace — 2026-10-07

1. **2026-04-05, #21 (`6dbcc0c`):** the branch's OWN ordering restriction — a branch pattern is the complete input specification, so a branch body infers nothing and Grace has nothing to reorder there. The same commit already processed algorithms nested in a branch "normally" (their own inference).
2. **Until 2026-08-09 (`7075071f`, #143):** one `Expr.Block` node covered both transparent `(…)` groups and scope-owning `{…}` blocks; the #21 parser scan descended into every `Expr.Block` without consulting `IsParametrized`. The #143 split into `Capture` / `AlgorithmExpr` translated that descent mechanically, so the scan kept rejecting an inline block's OWN markers — a representation side effect, not a decision — while a named property of the branch, never scanned, was accepted (X-08, PV-28).
3. **2026-09-13, F10 (`aaae65c`):** a marker on a FIXED binding is `InvalidGraceMarker` ("GRACE MUST BE EFFECTIVE … never a silent no-op"); its own suite called zero-movement markers on free names "EffectiveGrace" — the rule meant eligibility, but the wording read as displacement (X-39).
4. **2026-09-29, PV-49:** the scan read every row a branch writes; the detector's branch region stayed `NotReported` on the premise that the parser had reported every marker (PV-49's recommendation already named "a ConditionalBranch Grace policy in the detector" as the one owner).
5. **2026-10-07, investigation (`../q16-grace-investigation/final-report.md`, DECISION READY):** G-O recommended; M (movement required) and L (lexical ban) rejected after 13 falsification probes, 378 generated variants on six routes, the 23 Grace-bearing canonical sources, the full suite under each policy and a Lean differential.
6. **2026-10-07, owner decision: ADOPTS G-O** — Q-16(1) E and Q-16(2) O. **Implementation (same day, working tree over `66367a66`):** the parser scan is deleted; `GraceEffectPolicy.ClosedBranch` replaces `NotReported`; eligibility wording; `ApplyGraceReordering` unchanged; Lean docstrings narrowed; 87 previously rejected probe programs accepted, none rejected, no signature or value change (`../q16-grace-implementation/compatibility.md`).

**Surviving semantics.** Grace belongs to the owner whose written rows contain the marked occurrence (root, property body, brace block in any position, clause-branch body; `WrittenRows`, so hoisting never moves an occurrence). A marker is valid exactly when the occurrence becomes one of that owner's OWN inferred parameters; its weight is applied as far as the ordering allows; saturation is never an error. Fixed bindings and every occurrence on a closed level (a written list; a branch's own rows) are `InvalidGraceMarker`. A branch is closed at its own level only; nested inferring owners keep their Grace in every spelling and never add a parameter to the branch. In a load-bearing branch (MOD-10) the own-level verdict comes when the deferred unit is selected.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "Grace is not allowed in conditional branch bodies" (the lexical ban); "GRACE MUST BE EFFECTIVE … never a silent no-op" as a displacement requirement; "a marker that could reorder nothing is an ERROR"; "Grace has no effect on 'x' because …" as the current message; "the parser rejects every marker in every row a branch writes" (the detector does, for the branch's own rows only); "the detector strips branch markers without a report (`NotReported`)".

**Not decided here:** candidate X-49 — PAR-06's ordering prose does not fully determine `ApplyGraceReordering`'s multi-marker order (`K = a * 100 + b~ * 10 + ~~c` is `K(a, c, b)`, `K = a * 100 + b * 10 + ~~c` is `K(c, a, b)`); recorded open. *(Decided 2026-10-08: § X-49 below.)*

## X-49 — Grace movement order — 2026-10-08

1. **2016, US 9,417,850 FIG. 17:** the patent's loop repeatedly takes the FIRST UNMARKED parameter of the current list, moves it one step when its neighbour in its direction has a strictly less extreme current weight (a step consumes one unit of the mover's weight; the passed parameter keeps its own), and marks it otherwise; marks are never cleared. FIG. 12 (`a~~ + b~` is `(b, a)`) gives leftover weight its blocking meaning.
2. **2021, v0.6 implementation (unchanged until 2026-10-08 as `ParameterDetector.ApplyGraceReordering`):** a POSITION cursor follows the mover instead of re-selecting the first unmarked parameter; a parameter passed by a right-mover falls behind the cursor and never takes its own turn — a deviation from FIG. 17, not a property of the patented design.
3. **2026-10-07, Q-16:** candidate X-49 recorded — PAR-06's prose does not determine multi-marker orders (`K = a * 100 + b~ * 10 + ~~c` is `K(a, c, b)` while without `b~` it is `K(c, a, b)`).
4. **2026-10-08, first investigation (`../x49-grace-ordering-investigation/final-report.md`):** recommended the closed-form Target Order (sort by `(i + w, w)`) — NOT ADOPTED: the owner treats Grace as a movement operator (one marker, one adjacent exchange; markers accumulate; opposite markers cancel; movement can be blocked or saturated) and puts monotonicity first.
5. **2026-10-08, movement follow-up (`../x49-grace-ordering-investigation/movement-followup/final-report.md`):** front-first movement recommended — monotone (0 violations on every domain), equal weights stable, no skipped turn, no movement lost to timing, groups move as units, both one-direction recipes exact, all of the patent's worked examples.
6. **2026-10-08, owner decision: ADOPTS front-first movement with POSTFIX movers first**, the patent's strict remaining-weight comparison, retained residual weights and exact integer weights. **Implementation (same day, working tree over `f314cf67`):** `GraceMovement` replaces `ApplyGraceReordering`; weights become `BigInteger` end to end in the detector (the int-saturating `GraceWeightEffect` is deleted; the shared-node memo keeps exact per-visit deltas); `X49Witness_FollowsFrontFirstMovement`; `GraceMovementLawTests`; the `grace-front-first-movement` spec case; a standalone Lean model `lean/CoreTests/GraceMovement.lean`. Q-16 G-O eligibility, grammar, lifting and evaluation are unchanged.

**Surviving semantics.** An owner's OWN inferred names start in first semantic occurrence with their exact summed weights. Every name with a positive weight takes one turn, from the last-occurring to the first-occurring; then every name with a negative weight, from the first-occurring to the last-occurring; the schedule is fixed by the first-occurrence identities and initial weights. A turn exchanges the name with its neighbour one unit at a time until its remaining weight is zero, it reaches the end of the own list, or the neighbour moves the same way with at least as much REMAINING weight (compared on current remaining weights, before the step). A passed name keeps its weight; unused weight stays and keeps blocking; the lifted tail follows unchanged; at most n(n − 1) exchanges. `K = s * 100 + ~x * 10 + ~y` is `K(x, y, s)`; `Z = s~ * 100 + x~ * 10 + y` is `Z(y, s, x)`; `K = a~ * 100 + b * 10 + ~c` is `K(b, c, a)`; `F = ~a * 100 + b * 10 + ~~c` is `F(a, c, b)`.

**Current group consequence (2026-10-08, independent corrective review F1).** Equal accumulated weights preserve their original relative order. A contiguous equal-weight run moves as a unit when every parameter outside that run has zero weight. Other moving parameters can split the run while preserving its relative order. `K = a~ * 1000 + b~ * 100 + ~c * 10 + ~d` takes `(c, a, d, b)` and `K(1, 2, 3, 4)` is `2413`, so both original runs become noncontiguous. Step 5's unqualified group claim above is historical investigation wording, superseded by this narrower consequence; the adopted law is unchanged.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "the exact multi-marker iteration is the implementation's"; "a name swapped left by an earlier right-mover takes no turn of its own" as current behaviour; "a move stops at a neighbour with an equal or more extreme weight" as the complete rule (the comparison is on REMAINING weights and the schedule is the two passes); Target Order (`(i + w, w)`) as the ordering law; prefix-first movement; the patent's "first unmarked parameter" scheduling as the ordering law; int-saturated or clamped weights; "a saturated marker means exactly what the unmarked program means" (residual weight still blocks).

## VAR-03 + PAT-05 — collectors preserve supplied cells; empty structural patterns — 2026-10-09

### VAR-03

1. **2026-07-20 · 245b10c (no issue):** the function-shaped check — a collected argument with no value whose algorithm is callable-shaped is the collector's own `TypeMismatch` "collects values, but a supplied argument is a callable" (Lean `Algorithm.isFunctionShaped` in the collector arm of `bindParameterPatternList`; C# `IsFunctionShapedAlgorithm`). Collecting is a binding-time VALUE demand, so a failed argument fails the call.
2. **2026-09-28 · Q-03:** "callable-shaped" narrowed to "an ordinary zero-argument call cannot bind it"; a failed read of a zero-argument-acceptable callable surfaces its own error. The rule text the Constitution then held as VAR-03 is preserved verbatim below.
3. **2026-10-02 · Model C (NEED-01..10, implemented and V3 verified):** a collector binds a lazy exact slice of suspended cells; re-spreading a known slice transfers the cells "and their available VALUE/CALLABLE channels" (NEED-07, NEED-08/NEED-FWD); a collector's VALUE materializes every element. The collector's binding-time demand and its `TypeMismatch` disappeared from both implementations, and the renamed C# tests pinned the element's own error. The Model-C annex listed the rules it superseded — VAR-03 was not among them, so its value-only text survived as current law.
4. **2026-10-09 · constitution-implementation audit (M-02):** VAR-03 contradicted by NEED-07/08 and the implementation (`Fwd(*fs) = Apply(fs*)` / `Fwd(Inc)` = 10; `Coll(Bad)` with an unused collector = 1; `Collect(Inc)` the element's own `ArityMismatch`); classified OWNER DECISION REQUIRED.
5. **2026-10-09 · owner decision: ADOPTS the existing NEED-07/08 behavior.** A collecting parameter preserves the supplied demandable argument cells; a known collected slice can be explicitly re-spread, transporting the original cells and their available VALUE/CALLABLE capabilities without forcing VALUE; the collector creates no capability; the forwarding edge evaluates no VALUE. No C# or Lean behavior changed: the record is `../var03-pat05-reconciliation/` (102 witnesses with independent expectations on six routes; the 85 Lean-modeled ones agree with the authoritative Lean evaluator, 5 more use the unmodeled `trace` host operation and 12 are front-end rejections; a four-mutant discrimination check) with the new pins `CollectingCallableForwardingLawTests`, Lean `CoreTests/CollectingCallableForwarding.lean` and the spec case `collected-callable-survives-explicit-respread`.

**The superseded rule text (VAR-03 as held from 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-09; kept as history, not law):**

> ### VAR-03 — A collecting binding collects values, never callables
>
> **Class:** TYPE/KIND RULE, BINDING RULE
> **Status:** Current — see open question
> **Rule:** A collecting binding binds its name on the VALUE channel only. The collected list's elements are values, and a collected element can never be called. Each allocated item is handled as follows:
> - An item that has a value contributes that value. This includes a callable that accepts zero supplied arguments: a zero-parameter property, a brace block, or a collecting-only algorithm. Such a callable is value-demanded.
> - An item with no value whose algorithm is callable-shaped is a `TypeMismatch` at binding. Callable-shaped means that an ordinary call supplying zero arguments cannot bind it: a builtin, a clause family without a zero-arity branch (every family written in source), or an algorithm that requires a supplied argument. Declaring a parameter does not make a callable (Q-03): an item whose algorithm accepts zero supplied arguments, a collecting-only one included, is a value, and when its evaluation fails it surfaces its own error under the next bullet.
> - Any other item with no value surfaces its own error. Examples are a failed evaluation and an output-less written block (F5 blame).
>
> Unlike a fixed parameter, a collector never accepts a failed argument by binding only its algorithm channel.

It originated under the eager, value-only collector (steps 1–2) and was not reconciled when NEED-07/08 became current (step 3).

**Surviving semantics.** A collecting binding binds an exact slice of the supplied cells. Collecting demands nothing; re-spreading a known slice (`name*` on a parameter retaining a collector cell, including one transported whole through a fixed parameter; bare forwarding of a collecting source into a collecting destination) transfers the original cells with their available VALUE and CALLABLE capabilities, unforced; reading the collector as a value materializes one exact list, demanding every element by its own VALUE contract, so a callable element reports its own zero-argument demand verdict. The collector itself has no CALLABLE identity, and nothing passing through it gains one. Every other spread operand is evaluated during supply formation; static checks, cardinality, bare forwarding's by-name selection, Q-04 ownership and the PAT-06 kinds are unchanged.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "a collecting binding collects values, never callables"; "a collected element can never be called"; "a callable-shaped item is a `TypeMismatch` at binding" or any collector-specific error; "unlike a fixed parameter, a collector never accepts a failed argument"; "collectors surface a failed argument at the call"; `Coll(Fam)` / `Head(1, Fam)` as `TypeMismatch` (PAT-11's former collector-slot exception); "every callable-shaped collected argument is reported at binding".

### PAT-05

1. **Until 2026-09-29:** the pattern grammar had literals, binders and parenthesized groups; PAT-05 recorded "`F(1 + 1)`, `F(())` and `F([])` are parse errors" and "Empty and list patterns do not exist (e07, e08 → UnexpectedToken)".
2. **2026-09-29 · the structural-pattern decision (PAT-06):** list patterns `[ … ]` joined both pattern languages, and `()` and `[]` became distinct, valid structural patterns (`KatLang.ebnf` `SequencePattern = "(" [ Pattern ] ")"`, `ListPattern = "[" [ Pattern ] "]"`). PAT-06 and its Normal example (`Kind([])`, `Kind(())`) were updated; PAT-05's two sentences were not.
3. **2026-10-09 · audit (M-03):** PAT-05 contradicts PAT-06, the parser, the tutorial and the spec corpus.
4. **2026-10-09 · correction (no decision needed; no behavior change):** PAT-05 now prohibits general expressions in pattern positions and states that `()` and `[]` are valid, distinct structural patterns. Pins: `EmptyStructuralPatternLawTests`, Lean `CoreTests/EmptyStructuralPatterns.lean`, spec cases `empty-structural-patterns-are-distinct-heads` and `expression-is-not-a-pattern`.

**Surviving semantics.** Patterns use the pattern grammar, never general expression syntax: binders, a collecting binder where VAR-02 allows one, number (optionally negative), string and Boolean literals, and structural patterns, the empty `()` and `[]` included. An arithmetic expression or a call is a front-end error. `()` matches only the empty sequence and `[]` only the empty list; they are different heads, never duplicates.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "`F(())` and `F([])` are parse errors"; "Empty and list patterns do not exist"; "pattern atoms are limited to binders, `[-]`number, string, Boolean and `( … )`".

## Model-C foundations (Phase A1) — eager acquisition text reconciled — 2026-10-09

### The chain

1. **Until 2026-10-02 · the eager acquisition era.** CALL-02 evaluated every written argument slot once, left to right, at assembly, before any binding decision; CALL-03 gave builtins a separate adapter (spread slots first, collection value and surplus items evaluated at assembly behind the arity verdict, Math wrappers evaluating every argument before validating); CALL-06 (Q-01, 2026-09-28) retained an algorithm-channel slot's ordinary failure and failed a slot without one at assembly; RUN-07 (c) and RUN-08 listed those two retention points as the only places a failure went unraised.
2. **2026-10-02 · Model C (NEED-01..10, implemented and V3-verified):** one supply substrate for every callee — suspended cells in the caller's environment, arbitrary spreads formed first, cardinality before any VALUE demand, first-demand evaluation at most once, demand order deciding effects, CALLABLE projection and forwarding without force (call-by-need closeout and production reconciliation). The annex said it superseded the acquisition assumptions of CALL-02/03/04/06, PAT-07/09/10, PAR-04/07, FWD-01/02, HO-04, RUN-03/07/08 and RAND-01 "to the extent stated", but the rule texts were not rewritten, SUP-01, VAL-05, VAL-10, BOOL-05 and PROP-09 were not on its list, and its sentence "The 175 indexed rule entries and prior eager records remain historical evidence" made the override illegible.
3. **2026-10-03 · pre-release re-baseline:** Q-07 (one acquisition regime) and Q-08 (argument names resolved on demand) RESOLVED by later law; the CALL and BOOLCMP topic lists were not updated, so CALL-03's status kept pointing at a resolved question.
4. **2026-10-06 · Q-29 (A-U):** a written name that reaches an open level with two providers is a static `AmbiguousOpen`, whatever evaluation demands — superseding BOOL-05's and CALL-02's run-time name-resolution examples a second time.
5. **2026-10-09 · constitution-implementation audit (M-04):** about thirty rules still state eager outcomes; executed witnesses confirm the implementation and Lean follow Model C (`../constitution-implementation-audit-20261009/mismatches.md`).
6. **2026-10-09 · Phase A1 reconciliation (no owner decision; no behavior change):** CALL-02, CALL-03, CALL-06, SUP-01, VAL-05, VAL-10, RUN-03, RUN-08 and BOOL-05 (rule texts), RUN-07 (c) (its dependent list), RUN-01 and PROP-09 (examples and caveats) now state Model C; CALL-02, CALL-03 and CALL-06 are retitled; CALL-03's status is Current; the CALL and BOOLCMP topic lists mark Q-07/Q-08 resolved, and the SUP and RUN lists' pointers to them say so; the annex sentence is clarified. Every changed example was re-executed on six routes against independently derived expectations and, where modeled, against Lean (`../constitution-model-c-a1-reconciliation/`).

### The superseded rule texts (kept as history, not law)

CALL-02's former title: "A user call assembles one argument supply: every written slot evaluated once, left to right, in the caller's context, before any binding decision". Its former rule:

> **Rule:** For a user-defined callee (flat fixed, collecting or mixed, patterned, or clause family), the argument supply is complete before any arity check, clause selection, or pattern binding.
> - Written slots are evaluated left to right, each exactly once at assembly, directly in the CALLER's context. An argument list owns no scope.
> - Evaluation is eager: a slot the callee never reads is still evaluated.
> - A non-spread slot contributes exactly one item (see SUP: one value per non-spread slot). A spread slot contributes the items of one boundary (see SUP).
> - A written slot never disappears from the supply. A written argument whose expression has no output fails as THAT argument (`MissingOutput`) whenever its value is needed; it is never treated as an omitted argument.
> - No callee shape receives a second, written-slot view of a slot.

CALL-03's former title: "A builtin callee uses its own argument adapter: spread slots are forced first, non-spread slots are demanded by the builtin". Its former status "Current — see open question" and rule:

> **Rule:** A call whose selected callee is a builtin does not use CALL-02's assembly. Its written slots go through the builtin argument adapter.
> - **Which callables are builtins.** Only the 21 prelude builtins of the Lean model use the adapter (`Builtin`, lean/KatLang.lean:447-448; C# `BuiltinId`, Ast.cs:114). Math functions, their lowercase aliases, `random`/`randomInt` and host operations are C#-only prelude USER wrappers over `Expr.NativeCall`, so they bind through CALL-02: every argument is evaluated, left to right, before the native validates any of them.
> - **Non-sequence builtins** (`if`, `while`, `repeat`, `range`, `atoms`):
>   - EVERY spread slot is evaluated first, left to right among the spread slots, and expanded into ordinary slots.
>   - The builtin's arity is then checked against the expanded count, before any non-spread slot is evaluated.
>   - Non-spread slots stay unevaluated. The builtin demands its value slots (through CALL-05) or invokes its step slots, in its own order. A slot the builtin does not select is never evaluated.
>   - Each value slot is demanded AND validated before the next one is demanded: the `if` condition before any branch, the `repeat` count before the initial state (LOOP-05), and the `range` start before the stop.
> - **Collection builtins** (a collection plus controls): the written slots are assembled left to right, each by the ROLE its position has in the builtin's metadata (`SequenceBuiltinMetadata.slotRole` / `SlotRole`):
>   - a VALUE slot — the collection and every value or whole-number control (`contains`'s `item`, `take`/`skip`'s `count`, `reduce`'s `initial`) — is demanded ONCE, at assembly in written order (through CALL-05 for a callable-shaped argument). Its outcome, a value or an ORDINARY failure retained until binding reads the slot, is final and never retried;
>   - a CALLBACK slot — the `map` mapper, the `filter` predicate, the `reduce` reducer — receives the argument's algorithm channel and named callable and is never value-evaluated merely because it was supplied; the builtin invokes it per element (HO-02, HO-04). A callback slot with no CALLABLE identity reports `NotAnAlgorithm` when the builtin first attempts to invoke it (Q-06, decided 2026-10-05);
>   - a SPREAD slot is supply assembly: its operand is evaluated at once and either supplies exactly its items, which take the roles of the positions they land on, or its failure, of any kind, is the call's failure, raised before the arity check and before any later slot (SUP-02);
>   - a SURPLUS position (past the signature) keeps a value slot's eager evaluation, and the call's arity verdict follows every written item.

CALL-06's former title: "A written argument slot is evaluated at most once for its value and its outcome is final for the call; a retained failure fails the call only if that value is demanded". Its former rule (rules-only edition; the draft added the dated Q-02 parenthetical "(Until the Q-02 decision of 2026-09-28 this bullet read "An ordinary failure and a resource-limit failure are retained alike.")" to its resource-limit bullet):

> **Rule:** Within one call, a written argument slot is evaluated AT MOST ONCE for its value. If that evaluation succeeds, that is its value. If it fails with an ordinary error, that is its failure. If it reaches a resource limit, the call and the run end there: a resource limit is never a slot's outcome (RUN-03). Reading the bound parameter never causes the argument expression to execute again: argument evaluation uses the proper semantic route once (a named property through its ordinary property access and cache, a brace block through its own evaluation, a dot expression through ordinary dot resolution), and every parameter read reuses the outcome it established. That outcome is immutable for the lifetime of the call activation. A builtin value demand preserves a parameter's established failure, including its kind and payload, before considering the independent callable channel's signature.
> - Some non-spread argument slots also resolve to an algorithm: a name (property or parameter), a brace block, or a dot expression. When such a slot's value evaluation fails with an ordinary error, the failure is RETAINED, not raised: the slot binds its algorithm channel TOGETHER WITH that failure, and the call proceeds. Later slots are still evaluated.
> - A slot with no algorithm channel fails the call immediately at assembly. That covers literals, operator expressions, calls, lists, captures and spreads.
> - The retained failure surfaces only when something demands the parameter's value: a value-position read, a builtin value slot, the `.string` receiver, a native (Math, random, host) wrapper's argument read, a collector, a nested structural pattern, a repeated parameter name (PAT-09), a clause family, or a forwarding call whose slot is then demanded. Every such demand reports the SAME failure and none re-evaluates the argument, so a failure cannot heal, the argument's effects and random draws are never repeated, and one parameter never has two values in one activation.
> - Only an ORDINARY failure is retained. A slot whose evaluation reaches a resource limit fails the call at assembly whatever channels it carries, before any later slot is evaluated and before the callee runs, and the run ends with that limit (RUN-03).
> - The algorithm channel stays usable where the language uses it: invoking the parameter (`f(x)`, `f()`, an invoking builtin slot) is an ordinary invocation, and an explicit call is fresh (PROP-06); structural member access through the parameter (`o.X`) navigates the algorithm (DOT-02). Invoking never repairs or replaces the recorded value outcome.
> - The retained failure belongs to the SLOT of that call activation, not to the property the slot named. A failed evaluation is never cached (PROP-09), so a separate later demand of the property evaluates it afresh under PROP-04.

SUP-01's former sentence: "Each slot's expression is evaluated exactly once. Evaluation order is written order, except for the builtin argument regime owned by CALL-03 (see Known tension)."

VAL-05's former bullet:

> - Demanding its value anywhere fails with `MissingOutput`, and spreading it fails with `SpreadMissingOutput`. Demands include reading, comparing, counting, collecting, passing it to a value slot, and calling it. That failure is an ordinary failure, not a value (VAL-10).

VAL-10's former bullets: "A failure is not a sixth value kind. It cannot be bound, stored in a property, passed as an argument value, collected, compared, selected, spread or tested." (kept, with a sentence added); "The reported failure is the first one RAISED in evaluation order (see CALL-02, OP-03, CMP-02, PAT-10)."; the demand point "an argument whose ordinary failure is retained on the algorithm channel and never read as a value (CALL-06; a read reports the retained failure, and nothing re-derives it)"; and "Completed run state survives a failure: cache entries that nested reads stored successfully are kept (PROP-09)." (kept, with a sentence added).

RUN-03's former bullet:

> - **Never postponed or absorbed.** No construct can defer, absorb or replace it: not an unused parameter, a retained algorithm channel, a deferred value demand, forwarding, a builtin's arity verdict, an earlier retained ordinary failure, or a consumer's choice. A resource limit is therefore never a slot's recorded outcome (CALL-06) and never one of the deferred failures of RUN-07 (c). This is what separates it from an ORDINARY failure, which an argument slot still records once and a callee may leave undemanded (CALL-06).

and, in its limit-law bullet, "An actually encountered limit ends evaluation even if an earlier ordinary failure remains latent."

RUN-08's former rule (rules-only edition; the draft's copy differed only by the dated Q-01 parenthetical of its exactly-once sentence, which the draft keeps):

> **Rule:** A demanded expression evaluates its subexpressions eagerly, in the orders fixed by CALL-02, CALL-03, OP-03, BOOL-04, CMP-02, SEQ-02 and SEQ-05.
>
> Written code may go UNEVALUATED only at these points, and nowhere else:
> - a property body, until it is demanded; a cache hit re-runs nothing (PROP-02, PROP-04);
> - a deconstruction right-hand side, until one of its targets is demanded (VAR-06);
> - the unselected branch of builtin `if` (BOOL-05);
> - the non-spread slots of the non-sequence builtins (`if`, `while`, `repeat`, `range`, `atoms`) that the builtin does not demand: each value slot is demanded and validated before the next, after the arity check, so a slot after a failed validation is never reached (CALL-03);
> - invoking slots, which are never value-demanded: a callback is invoked once per element (HO-02, HO-04) and a loop step once per iteration (LOOP-05, LOOP-06, LOOP-08); supplying one evaluates nothing, so an unused callback has no effect (a collection builtin's callback slot value-evaluated an argument that declares no parameters until 2026-09-29, PV-19);
> - the step of a zero-count `repeat` (LOOP-05);
> - unselected clause bodies (PAT-02);
> - deferred module branches, whose modules are fetched and elaborated only when selected (MOD-10);
> - `open` providers, which opening neither activates nor evaluates (MOD-04);
> - structural dot navigation, which evaluates nothing (DOT-02).
>
> A FAILURE may go unraised at two further points, both listed in RUN-07 (c): an algorithm-channel argument is evaluated eagerly, but its ORDINARY failure is retained until its value is demanded (CALL-06); and a collection builtin's value or surplus item is evaluated at assembly, its ORDINARY failure retained until binding reads the slot, behind the arity verdict (CALL-03). Retaining is not re-evaluating: the demand reports the failure the slot already established. A resource-limit failure is never retained: the eager evaluation that reaches it ends the run (RUN-03).
>
> Everything else is strict:
> - user-call arguments, even those the callee never reads (CALL-02);
> - both operands of every operator: there is no short circuit (OP-03, BOOL-04);
> - every comparison operand, eagerly past a `false` link (CMP-02);
> - list, capture and row slots (SUP-01, SEQ-02, VAL-07);
> - spread operands in every call: a spread slot is evaluated while the supply is assembled, and its failure is raised there, before any arity check or binding (SUP-02, CALL-02, CALL-03);
> - collection builtins, which evaluate the whole collection: `first(map([1, 2, 3], {trace(x)}))` invokes all three elements (COLL-04 caveat; HO-02).
>
> No optimizer, route or future builtin may add a deferral point: that would be a language change, not an optimization (RUN-01).
>
> "Each evaluated subexpression is evaluated once per evaluation of its parent" has exactly these exceptions (a written call argument is NOT one of them: within one call a slot is evaluated at most once for its value, and reading its parameter never evaluates it again — CALL-06):
> - re-evaluation of a failed property on each later read, since failures are never cached (PROP-09);
> - re-evaluation of a failed deconstruction right-hand side on each later demand (VAR-06; a successful one runs at most once);
> - every explicit call `A()`, which is fresh (PROP-06);
> - one invocation per element or iteration for callbacks and loop steps.

BOOL-05's former step 1, "Spread arguments are expanded (and so evaluated) first, by the builtin argument adapter (CALL-03).", and paragraph: "This laziness belongs to the resolved builtin identity. It holds for every spelling that reaches that identity (`if(c, t, e)`, `c.if(t, e)`, and a parameter bound to `if` and called with written arguments). It disappears when `if` is shadowed. It never reaches back to values that were already evaluated before selection: values supplied by a spread slot (step 1), or arguments a caller or a wrapper has already evaluated. So in `if(args*)` nothing is lazy for the slots the spread supplies; only the non-spread slots of such a call stay lazy."

RUN-07 (c)'s former text (identical in both editions; its last paragraph is kept in the new (c) as history):

> - **(c) The closed list of places where a failure is not raised at once.** ORDINARY failures are DEFERRED (retained on a binding) only at:
>   - algorithm-channel argument slots (CALL-06; the failure surfaces only when the value is demanded, and every demand reports that same retained failure — it is never re-derived);
>   - collection-builtin value and surplus items whose arity verdict wins (CALL-03: `count(1 / 0, 2)` is `ArityMismatch`); a failed SPREAD is never deferred: it is raised during assembly (SUP-02).
>
>   (Until 2026-09-29 the list also named "the builtin callback value-thunk fall-through": a callback slot's argument was value-evaluated during assembly and its failure dropped, and `reduce`'s `initial`, typed as a callback, was then retried. A callback slot now never evaluates its argument, so nothing fails there to be deferred — `map([1, 2], 1 / 0)` is the invocation's `ArityMismatch`, HO-04's known tension — and `initial` is a value slot: PV-05, PV-19 and PV-20 resolved.)

The annex's former sentence: "The 175 indexed rule entries and prior eager records remain historical evidence; this annex is the current production acquisition contract."

The byte-exact pre-edit files are in the F3 archive recorded in `../constitution-model-c-a1-reconciliation/preservation-f3.md`.

**Surviving semantics.** Forming a call's supply evaluates only its arbitrary explicit spreads (left to right among them); every other argument is a suspended computation of the caller, evaluated at most once on its first VALUE demand, and never if undemanded. Cardinality is checked before any such demand, for every callee category. The order of first demands decides the order of argument effects, draws and failures. Binding, transport, forwarding, collecting and CALLABLE projection demand nothing; invoking a callable is fresh. Operators, output rows, list and capture construction, inspecting patterns, a collector's VALUE and collection builtins stay strict. A demanded failure ends the run, a demanded computation keeps its completed outcome for later demands, a reached resource limit or cancellation ends the run, and static validation never depends on demand. Builtin `if` demands its condition and only the selected branch, through wrappers and aliases too; a shadowing callee demands what its body demands.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "every written slot evaluated once, left to right … before any binding decision"; "a slot the callee never reads is still evaluated"; a builtin callee "uses its own argument adapter" for acquisition (it forms its supply like every call); "a slot with no algorithm channel fails the call immediately at assembly"; an ordinary failure "retained on the algorithm channel" at assembly; "Everything else is strict: user-call arguments, even those the callee never reads"; collection-builtin value or surplus items evaluated before the arity verdict; a Math wrapper evaluating every argument before validating; "shadowing or wrapping removes the laziness"; every slot's algorithm channel resolved before any slot is evaluated; argument retention as a way to observe that a failed property is not cached; "the 175 indexed rule entries … remain historical evidence".

## Model-C Phase A1 independent review — terminal completion wording — 2026-10-09

The independent review found two A1 statements that confused run terminality with demand-cell storage. The adopted NEED-02/NEED-09 laws and production behavior already prevent restarting terminal completion. No semantic policy changed.

Superseded A1 wording, preserved verbatim:
- CALL-06: "If it reaches a resource limit, the run ends there: a resource limit is never a slot's outcome (RUN-03)."
- RUN-08: "A resource-limit failure is never kept: the evaluation that reaches it ends the run (RUN-03)."
- CALL-06: "A failed evaluation is never cached (PROP-09), and a separate demand of the property"

Current replacement: a reached limit ends the run; its terminal completion cannot restart work or become a recoverable argument value. CALL-06 distinguishes completed cell failure from the uncached failed PROPERTY evaluation. This narrows wording to NEED-09 and NEED-10, rather than changing terminality or caching. C# `NeedCell.Complete` stores completion and retains the terminal budget; `ResourceFailureDuringFirstDemand_IsStickyAndStopsOtherCells` checks sync/async first demand, preserved error/span, no restart, no callable projection and no work in another cell. Resource limits remain a C# operational extension, not a Lean-core modeling claim.

The original A1 reports and both F3 archives remain unchanged. The original witness judge accepted an invalid expectation string (`garbage`) as PASS; the independent review preserves that reproduction and supplies a schema-checked judge, with corrupted outcome/log and malformed-expectation discrimination. Its Lean comparator records the actual reached `unknownName` payload rather than excluding a mismatch merely from source spelling. Evidence: `../constitution-model-c-a1-independent-review/final-review.md`, `constitution-review.md`, `lean-alignment.md` and `raw/` therein. No Phase A2 item is implemented, no status changes, Q-25 stays open.

## Model-C propagation (Phase A2) — eager wording reconciled in 18 rules — 2026-10-09

Phase A1 (2026-10-09) reconciled Model C's foundations and named the rules whose own text still described the pre-Model-C acquisition. Phase A2 restates those eighteen — DOT-03, DOT-08, VAR-04, VAR-06, PAR-01, PAT-07, PAT-09, PAT-10, PROP-02, PROP-04, PROP-05, HO-01, HO-04, COLL-02, COLL-09, RUN-07, RAND-01, RAND-03 — and corrects the RES-03/LOOP-01 pointers and PAR-07's index title. No owner decision was taken and no C# or Lean behavior changed: Model C (NEED-01..10, NEED-FWD; adopted and implemented 2026-10-02) is the current law, and every changed example was re-executed on six C# routes against independently derived expectations (`../constitution-model-c-a2-reconciliation/witness-results.md`).

**Dated chain.** Q-01 (2026-09-28, at-most-once) → Q-02 (2026-09-28, limits terminal) → Model C (2026-10-02) → Q-07/Q-08/Q-21/Q-22 resolved by later law (2026-10-03) → Q-06, Q-18, Q-27 (2026-10-05) → Q-29 (2026-10-06) → Q-28 owner follow-up (2026-10-07) → Phase A1 (2026-10-09) → Phase A2 (2026-10-09).

**Surviving semantics.** A dot-call receiver is the call's first supplied computation; `.string(args)` is rejected by cardinality before any demand; a clause family demands what its ordered pattern inspection needs and binds both channels; a repeated name demands each occurrence's own cell when visited, and the first failure or conflict in written traversal order is reported (D1's cardinality-first rule and prefix/suffix allocation survive; its settle order does not); a deconstruction right-hand side runs on the first demand of a target; passing demands nothing, invoking is fresh, and a VALUE read of a named property is its cached read; native Math/random wrappers demand and validate one argument at a time; random draws follow formation then first demand for every callee.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "the receiver is evaluated exactly once, before the written arguments"; "`.string(args)` … each slot evaluated once, left to right"; "every argument is value-demanded before any clause is tried"; "family binders bind on the value channel only"; "every pattern binds, left to right, before any repeated name is decided"; "the collector collects first"; "innermost merge wins"; "a failing right-hand side … is evaluated again on the next demand"; "User-call arguments are evaluated eagerly, once, left to right, even when the callee ignores them"; "`Call0(A)` reads A's value for the argument"; "is additionally bound on the value channel, eagerly"; "Collection builtins evaluate every written value and surplus slot … before the arity verdict"; "`pow('a', 1/0)` → `DivisionByZero`"; "user calls left to right versus builtins spread-first"; "both arguments are evaluated before either is validated".

The Lean guard `testValueBinderShadowsCallerAlgorithm` uses a number. ownership-and-lookup.md § Parameter channels says a call binds "on the value channel, the algorithm channel, or both" and lists clause-family binders among the binding sites without saying they are value-only (w1-contradictions [L2], [D1]). Whether this is design or a leftover of the #39 sidestep is undecided (this topic's open question; CALL's PAR-01 and ALGHO's HO-01 questions point here). *Resolved 2026-10-03 (Q-21, by later law): NEED-04 (adopted and implemented 2026-10-02) supersedes this rule's value-only and first-order clauses — an argument is demanded only by the patterns that inspect it and the body that uses it, and a successful branch retains both channels of its bound cells — so a family receives a callable: `App(f, 0) = 0` / `App(f, n) = f(n)` / `R(z) = App(Inc, 5)` / `R(0)` is `6` on six routes, Lean agreeing. The formula-lifting role of a family's arguments stays VALUE (PAR-07, retained by NEED-05), so an INFERRING formula still lifts a bare callable written there (`R = App(Inc, 5)` is `R(y) = App(Inc(y), 5)`).*

- PAT-10 · constitution-draft.md · Rule:
  > **Rule:** When an ordinary pattern list could fail for more than one reason, the reported failure is fixed by the following order, in every execution path and in Lean:
  > 1. **The arity check** of the list.
  > 2. **Binding before settling:**
  >    - **Without a collector,** every pattern binds, left to right, before any repeated name is decided. This includes nested groups' value demands and arity checks, any retained argument error a pattern needs, and a repeated name's own value requirement (PAT-09: a valueless occurrence fails its own binding).
  >    - **With a collector,** the order is:
  >      1. the prefix binds and settles its own repeated names;
  >      2. the suffix does the same;
  >      3. the collector collects;
  >      4. only then are names shared across the collector decided.
  > 3. **Among repeated-name failures:**
  >    - the name whose deciding merge runs first is reported, that is, the innermost merge (the name completing furthest right);
  >    - within one merge, an unequal value (ArityMismatch, "repeated parameter … requires equal arguments") comes before a callable-identity conflict (TypeMismatch).
  >
  > A later binding failure therefore always outranks a repeated-name conflict in the same range.

- PROP-05 · constitution-draft.md · Rule:
  > **Rule:** The decision to reuse or evaluate belongs to the property ACCESS, never to the consumer. Every value consumer must receive the value that the one access produced. This covers operator and comparison operands, list and capture elements, selection `A:i`, spread `A*`, and user-call arguments in either spelling (`F(A)`, `A.F`) together with the parameter they bind, forwarded any number of times (the parameter reuses its argument slot's outcome, a failure included, and never re-runs the body: CALL-06). It covers every builtin VALUE slot in written, dotted, or grouped spelling (`sum(A)`, `A.sum`, `sum((A))`, `(A).count`, `take`, `first`, `range`/`atoms` arguments), the selected `if` branch and the condition, a loop's initial state and `repeat` count, `reduce`'s initial accumulator, the `.string` receiver (`A.string`, `Obj.A.string`, and a parameter's `v.string`), and a callback body that reads the property. No builtin has property-evaluation semantics different from a user algorithm's. The lifting positions among these consumers (operands, list elements, `A:i`, `A*`, registry-strict Math arguments) receive the one access for every callable that accepts zero supplied arguments, a collecting-only one included, because the front end never lifts it into a fresh call (PAR-07).

- HO-04 · constitution-draft.md · Rule:
  > - **Value slots.** Every VALUE slot reads the bound value, through the one cached property read (see PROP). The value slots are the collection, `reduce`'s `initial`, and a loop's initial state; each is demanded once and its outcome is final (`reduce`'s `initial` is a value control of the builtin metadata since 2026-09-29: formerly a failed first evaluation was dropped and retried, PV-05). A forwarded parameter whose argument slot FAILED is read the same way: the value slot reports the recorded failure and never re-runs the argument (CALL-06). Before the Q-01 decision of 2026-09-28 such a parameter reached a builtin value slot as its raw algorithm and was re-evaluated there: `G(v) = reduce([1], Add, v)` / `G(Bad)` with `Bad = trace(1) / 0` traced three times; it now traces once.

- HO-04 · constitution-summary.md · Rule:

The value slots are the collection, `reduce`'s `initial`, and a loop's initial state; each is demanded once and its outcome is final (`reduce`'s `initial` is a value control of the builtin metadata since 2026-09-29: formerly a failed first evaluation was dropped and retried, PV-05). A forwarded parameter whose argument slot FAILED is read the same way: the value slot reports the recorded failure and never re-runs the argument (CALL-06).

- HO-04 · constitution-draft.md · Rule:
  > - **Value-only parameters.** A parameter bound on the value channel only has no callable to invoke. An invoking slot that receives it — or any other cell with no CALLABLE identity — reports `NotAnAlgorithm` when it is invoked, exactly as a user higher-order parameter does (Q-06, decided 2026-10-05); nothing is evaluated to find that out.

- COLL-02 · constitution-draft.md · Known tension:
  > **Known tension:** Collection builtins evaluate every written value and surplus slot (never a callback slot) before the arity verdict and retain those slots' ordinary errors (a slot that reaches a resource limit ends the run at once, RUN-03; a failed spread is raised at once, SUP-02). So `count(1 / 0, 2)` is an `ArityMismatch` (and `count(trace(1), trace(2))` logs both traces first), while a user `F(x) = x; F(1 / 0, 2)` is `DivisionByZero`. `atoms`/`range`/`if` evaluate no non-spread slot on the arity path (w1 [C4] S4; this is AGENTS "argument-slot assembly is SHARED by every callable shape" versus the code; CALL owns it).

- COLL-09 · constitution-draft.md · Rule:
  > - **Order.** For written (non-spread) bounds, `start` is demanded and validated (whole number) before `stop` is demanded. So `range('a', 1/0)` → `TypeMismatch` and `stop` is never evaluated: `range(trace('a'), trace(1) / 0)` logs only `trace('a')`. This differs from operators (OP-03: both operands, then validation), from Math wrappers (`pow('a', 1/0)` → `DivisionByZero`), and from collection builtins, which evaluate every written slot before validating (`take('a', 1/0)` → `DivisionByZero`; CALL-03). Spread bounds are forced before either bound is demanded (CALL-03).

### A2-IR-01: PAT-09 (constitution-draft.md)

FWD-02 specifies target identity, not an inherited independent signature.

Previous text (superseded):

> - **Forwarded occurrences (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed).** *Repeated names constrain independently supplied arguments. When implicit forwarding supplies the same caller binding to several occurrences, each occurrence receives that same complete binding, and no synthetic value/callable merge occurs.* Formula forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns (PAR-07): `P(x, x) = x` / `D = P + 1` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly the written `Same(x) = P(x, x) + 1`. Each occurrence is an ordinary argument slot reading the caller's one binding — the value and callable of ONE argument, or that argument's completed failure (CALL-06) — so this rule holds by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure (`D(Inc)` is Inc's own value demand and `D(Bad)` is Bad's failure, evaluated once). An explicit call with its own parameters (`Both(a, b) = P(a, b)`) keeps the occurrences independent, as the direct `P(7, 8)` does, and so does the exact alias `Some = P`, which inherits `P(x, x)` verbatim (FWD-02): `Some(7, 8)` is `P(7, 8)`'s own failure and `Some(Bad, 7)` is Bad's. Bare forwarding follows the by-name rule of the formula: `Q(x) = P` hands Q's ONE binding `x` to both occurrences, `P(x, x)` (`Q(7)` gives `7`). (Until FWD-02's alias rule, 2026-09-29, this clause read `Some = P` as `Some(x) = P(x, x)`; for one day the positional reading made `Q(x) = P` the call `P(x)`.)

Current replacement:

> - **Forwarded occurrences (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed).** *Repeated names constrain independently supplied arguments. When implicit forwarding supplies the same caller binding to several occurrences, each occurrence receives that same complete binding, and no synthetic value/callable merge occurs.* Formula forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns (PAR-07): `P(x, x) = x` / `D = P + 1` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly the written `Same(x) = P(x, x) + 1`. Each occurrence is an ordinary argument slot reading the caller's one binding — the value and callable of ONE argument, or that argument's completed failure (CALL-06) — so this rule holds by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure (`D(Inc)` is Inc's own value demand and `D(Bad)` is Bad's failure, evaluated once). An explicit call with its own parameters (`Both(a, b) = P(a, b)`) keeps the occurrences independent, as the direct `P(7, 8)` does, and so does the callable alias `Some = P`, whose CALLABLE identity is `P` itself by binding indirection, with no signature of its own (FWD-02, adopted 2026-10-01): `Some(7, 8)` is `P(7, 8)`'s own failure and `Some(Bad, 7)` is Bad's. Bare forwarding follows the by-name rule of the formula: `Q(x) = P` hands Q's ONE binding `x` to both occurrences, `P(x, x)` (`Q(7)` gives `7`). When implicit forwarding supplies the same caller binding to several occurrences, each occurrence receives that same complete binding, and no synthetic value/callable merge occurs.* Formula forwarding is by binding name (PAR-07): `D = P + 1` with `P(x, x)` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly the written `Same(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, so the occurrences agree by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure. An explicit call with its own parameters (`Both(a, b) = P(a, b)`) keeps the occurrences independent, as the direct `P(7, 8)` does, and so does the exact alias `Some = P`, which inherits `P(x, x)` verbatim (FWD-02); bare forwarding `Q(x) = P` follows the formula's by-name rule, `P(x, x)`.

Current replacement:

> - **(c) Forwarded occurrences (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed):** *Repeated names constrain independently supplied arguments. When implicit forwarding supplies the same caller binding to several occurrences, each occurrence receives that same complete binding, and no synthetic value/callable merge occurs.* Formula forwarding is by binding name (PAR-07): `D = P + 1` with `P(x, x)` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly the written `Same(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, so the occurrences agree by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure. An explicit call with its own parameters (`Both(a, b) = P(a, b)`) keeps the occurrences independent, as the direct `P(7, 8)` does, and so does the callable alias `Some = P`, whose CALLABLE identity is `P` itself by binding indirection, with no signature of its own (FWD-02, adopted 2026-10-01); bare forwarding `Q(x) = P` follows the formula's by-name rule, `P(x, x)`.

### A2-IR-14: CALL-06 (constitution-draft.md)

Make the already adopted A1 law explicit in both editions; no law change.

Previous text (superseded):

> **Rule:** Within one call, a written argument slot is ONE supplied computation (CALL-02). It is evaluated AT MOST ONCE, when its VALUE is first demanded, in the caller's retained environment. If that evaluation succeeds, that is its value. If it fails with an ordinary error, that is its failure. If it reaches a resource limit, the run ends there: that terminal completion cannot restart work and is never a recoverable argument value (RUN-03, NEED-09). A slot whose VALUE is never demanded is never evaluated, so an unused argument cannot fail, run an effect or draw (NEED-01, NEED-03). The demand uses the proper semantic route once (a named property through its ordinary property access and cache, NEED-10; a brace block through its own evaluation; a dot expression through ordinary dot resolution), and every later demand reuses the outcome it established. That outcome is immutable for the lifetime of the call activation (NEED-02). A builtin value demand preserves a parameter's established failure, including its kind and payload, before considering the independent callable channel's signature.

## Model-C final reconciliation (Phase A3) — CALL-04, PAR-04, PAR-07, FWD-01 and FWD-02, and the remaining Model-C residue — 2026-10-10

Phase A2 (2026-10-09) left five rules whose own text still described the pre-Model-C acquisition — CALL-04, PAR-04, PAR-07, FWD-01 and FWD-02 (its `next-cohort.md`) — and handed over the Appendix A coverage rows, the remaining current-tense eager statements and their direct cross-references. Phase A3 restates the five in Model-C terms (NEED-01..10, NEED-FWD), corrects the residue a targeted sweep found in other rules, topic notes, Appendix A, the Model-C annex and two registry notes, and retitles FWD-01 (same ID). No owner decision was needed and no C# or Lean behavior changed; Q-45, Q-25 and X-18 stay open, and Q-37 is unchanged.

**Dated chain.** Q-01 (2026-09-28, at-most-once) → Q-02 (2026-09-28, limits terminal) → FWD-02's alias rule (2026-09-29) → the unified formula-lifting law (2026-09-30) → aliases as binding indirection, Q-12/Q-13/Q-77/Q-78 resolved (2026-10-01) → Model C, Q-15 resolved (2026-10-02, `8f0ceb85`) → Q-06/Q-27 (2026-10-05) → Q-28 owner follow-up (2026-10-07) → Phase A1, VAR-03 decision, Phase A2 and its independent review (2026-10-09) → Phase A3 (2026-10-10).

**Surviving semantics.** A parameter list counts supply cells; a count the selected callee does not accept is `ArityMismatch` before any non-spread demand, for every callee category, and a clause family reports `NoMatchingBranch` only for an accepted count that no clause matches; a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged, attaching its cell; the arity payload is (minimum supplied slots, complete supply count); a formula's lifting role is static and the lifted call is an ordinary supplied computation; a reference that a closed list blocks is its run-time zero-argument demand, never a static diagnostic; forwarding — a collector's re-spread, bare forwarding and every synthesized call — transfers supply cells unforced, with both channels; spread(collect(S)) = S holds for the cells and for their values; a callable alias is binding indirection; a reached resource limit is a demanded cell's terminal completion. Unchanged: by-name forwarding (Q-04, FWD-02), PAR-05's order, Q-03's zero-argument reads, Q-77's static `UnforwardableCallable`, X-02's signature rules and the D1 callback law.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "a wrong argument count selects no clause (NoMatchingBranch)"; "It never fails with ArityMismatch"; "`NoMatchingBranch` for a clause family, where a wrong argument count selects no clause"; "It is additionally a front-end `UndeclaredIdentifier` only in a registry-strict Math value position"; "a strict Math position is the front-end diagnostic"; "The static rejection of a blocked forwarding covers Math strict positions only"; "it appears where its immediate consumer demands its VALUE"; "Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread"; "A reference to a collected binding is just an ordinary list value"; "evaluates each forwarded binding exactly once"; "a reached limit is never a cell's completed outcome"; "Callback and direct calls use two binder implementations"; "Every written slot is evaluated once, left to right, in the caller's context, before binding"; "the value-tier payload `(1, 0)`"; "Unused user-call arguments are evaluated."

- CALL-01 · constitution-draft.md:1983 · Rule (under: CALL-01 — A call selects one callee identity first and binds against that callee's signatu)
  > - A supply that the selected signature cannot bind is an evaluation-time error: `ArityMismatch` for a user or builtin callee, and `NoMatchingBranch` for a clause family, where a wrong argument count selects no clause (see PAT-03(b)). It is never a parse-time error, and an unevaluated wrong-arity call is inert.
  Now:
  > - A supply that the selected signature cannot bind is an evaluation-time error: `ArityMismatch` for every callee category whose cardinality the supply misses — a user or builtin callee, and a clause family, whose wrong argument count no clause head accepts (NEED-05; see PAT-03(b)) — and `NoMatchingBranch` for a clause family supplied an accepted count that no clause matches (PAT-02). *(Until Model C, 2026-10-02, a family's wrong count was `NoMatchingBranch` too.)* It is never a parse-time error, and an unevaluated wrong-arity call is inert.

- CALL-01 · constitution-draft.md:2007 · Normal example (under: CALL-01 — A call selects one callee identity first and binds against that callee's signatu)
  > - `Pick(0, y) = y` / `Pick(x, y) = x` / `Pick(1, 2, 3)` is `NoMatchingBranch` "No matching branch for 'Pick'" (clause family; `CALL-final/c04.kat`). So are `Fam(1, 2)`, `Fam()` and a too-short `Fam(5)` against a two-slot family (`adv/h93`, `CALL-final/f01`, `adv/h95`).
  Now:
  > - `Pick(0, y) = y` / `Pick(x, y) = x` / `Pick(1, 2, 3)` is `ArityMismatch` "Property 'Pick' expects 2 parameters, but was called with 3 arguments." (clause family): the family's cardinality is checked before any clause is tried and before any argument is demanded (NEED-05), so `Pick(trace(1), trace(2), trace(3))` has an empty host log. So are `Fam(1, 2)` against a one-slot family, `Fam()` against any source family and a too-short `Fam(5)` against a two-slot family, while `P(0, y) = y` / `P(x, 0) = x` / `P(1, 1)` — an accepted count that no clause matches — is `NoMatchingBranch` "No matching branch for 'P'" (re-run 2026-10-10, Phase A3, six routes; Lean agrees). *(Until Model C, 2026-10-02, all of these were `NoMatchingBranch`: `CALL-final/c04.kat`, `adv/h93`, `CALL-final/f01`, `adv/h95`.)*

  Now:

- CALL-04 · constitution-draft.md:2177 · Rule (under: CALL-04 — Arity counts supplied items, and a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged in e)
  > - A parameter list is satisfied by the number of supplied ITEMS, never by the element count of any value.
  Now:
  > - A parameter list is satisfied by the number of supplied ITEMS, never by the element count of any value. The supplied items are the call's supply cells (CALL-02): one per non-spread written slot, whatever its kind or eventual VALUE, and one per item an explicit spread opens (NEED-01, NEED-07).

- CALL-04 · constitution-draft.md:2178 · Rule (under: CALL-04 — Arity counts supplied items, and a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged in e)
  > - A fixed parameter binds exactly one supplied item, unchanged, whatever its kind: a sequence, a list, `()` or `[]` stays one value.
  Now:
  > - A fixed parameter binds exactly one supplied item, unchanged, whatever its kind: a sequence, a list, `()` or `[]` stays one value. Binding attaches the item's cell without demanding it; when that VALUE is demanded it is the item's value, unchanged (NEED-01, NEED-04).

- CALL-04 · constitution-draft.md:2180 · Rule (under: CALL-04 — Arity counts supplied items, and a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged in e)
  > - A supplied count that the flat signature does not accept is `ArityMismatch`. This holds identically for the direct call `F(v)`, the dotted call `v.F` (see DOT), and a callback (see ALGHO). A failed spread supplies no item, so it never takes part in an arity verdict: its own failure is raised first (SUP-02).
  Now:
  > - A supplied count that the selected callee does not accept is `ArityMismatch`, raised before any non-spread supplied computation is demanded (NEED-05). This holds identically for the direct call `F(v)`, the dotted call `v.F` (see DOT), a callback (see ALGHO) and every callee category, a clause family included: a family rejects a count no clause head accepts as `ArityMismatch` before trying any clause, and reports `NoMatchingBranch` only for an accepted count that no clause matches (PAT-02, PAT-03). A failed spread supplies no item, so it never takes part in an arity verdict: its own failure is raised first (SUP-02).

- PAR-04 · constitution-draft.md:2511 · Rule (under: PAR-04 — An explicit parameter list is closed for its own level: nothing is inferred there)
  > A formula reference to a callable that accepts zero supplied arguments is never a forwarding candidate (PAR-07), so a closed list never blocks it and it is never that front-end error: it is the cached zero-argument value demand in every formula position. (A lone row names it as the callee instead, and bare forwarding supplies its collector from a compatible same-named binding: a fixed source contributes one whole item, and a collecting source re-spreads its items; otherwise it forwards nothing and the row reads the cached value: with `Only(*xs) = xs`, `F(p) = Only` / `F(3)` gives `[]`, FWD-02.)
  Now:
  > A formula reference to a callable that accepts zero supplied arguments is never a forwarding candidate (PAR-07), so a closed list never blocks it: it is the cached zero-argument value demand in every formula position. (A lone row names it as the callee instead, and bare forwarding supplies its collector from a compatible same-named binding: a fixed source contributes its one cell as one item, and a collecting source re-spreads its collected cells (NEED-08); otherwise it forwards nothing and the row reads the cached value: with `Only(*xs) = xs`, `F(p) = Only` / `F(3)` gives `[]`, FWD-02.)

- PAR-05 · constitution-draft.md:2573 · Rule (under: PAR-05 — An inferred signature lists the level's own names by first semantic occurrence, f)
  > Own names and lifted names are never interleaved. The order in which a runtime fallback assembles its call never determines the signature order. An exact alias (FWD-02) infers nothing: it inherits its callee's parameter patterns verbatim, and bare forwarding keeps its written list. A destination callable's parameter order never reorders an explicit source list: `F(y, x) = y - x` / `G(x, y) = F` keeps `G(x, y)` and supplies `F(y, x)` by name.
  Now:
  > Own names and lifted names are never interleaved. The order in which a runtime fallback assembles its call never determines the signature order. A callable alias (FWD-02) infers nothing: it has no signature of its own — its CALLABLE identity is its target's, by binding indirection (2026-10-01) — and bare forwarding keeps its written list. A destination callable's parameter order never reorders an explicit source list: `F(y, x) = y - x` / `G(x, y) = F` keeps `G(x, y)` and supplies `F(y, x)` by name.

- PAR-05 · constitution-draft.md:2575 · Boundary (under: PAR-05 — An inferred signature lists the level's own names by first semantic occurrence, f)
  > **Pattern-shape boundary (independent review, 2026-09-29; revised the same day by the structural-pattern model and then by FWD-02's alias rule):** Deduplication removes later captures, and a group keeps its KIND for the names that are new there. A sequence group left with ONE non-collecting binder is that binder, because the singleton `(x)` is not a pattern (PAT-06): `P((x, x)) = x` / `Some = [P]:0` infers `Some(x)` and calls `P((x, x))`, so `Some(v)` is the written `Some(x) = [P((x, x))]:0` for every `v` (`Some(7)` is `7`, `Some([7])` is `[7]`, `Some((7, 8))` is `(7, 8)`). A list group keeps its brackets: `P([x, x]) = x` / `Some = [P]:0` infers `Some([x])` and calls `P([x, x])` (`Some([7])` is `7`; `Some(7)` is TypeMismatch; `Some([7, 8])` ArityMismatch). A group left with no new binder contributes nothing. This follows the partial-group rule, not an exception for repeated names; a further formula forwards each surviving group as its own kind again (FWD-02). An exact alias is not inferred at all: `Some = P` inherits `P((x, x))` verbatim, so `Some((7, 7))` is `7` and `Some(7)` is the kind mismatch of `P(7)`. (Before FWD-02's alias rule these observations belonged to `Some = P`; before the structural-pattern model the sequence group survived as the one-item `Some((x))`, whose one-level opening made `Some([7])` `7`, and PV-08 had rebuilt it as a list.) C# tests pin inference and these observations; Lean evaluates the corresponding explicit trees and does not prove signature inference.
  Now:
  > **Pattern-shape boundary (independent review, 2026-09-29; revised the same day by the structural-pattern model and then by FWD-02's alias rule):** Deduplication removes later captures, and a group keeps its KIND for the names that are new there. A sequence group left with ONE non-collecting binder is that binder, because the singleton `(x)` is not a pattern (PAT-06): `P((x, x)) = x` / `Some = [P]:0` infers `Some(x)` and calls `P((x, x))`, so `Some(v)` is the written `Some(x) = [P((x, x))]:0` for every `v` (`Some(7)` is `7`, `Some([7])` is `[7]`, `Some((7, 8))` is `(7, 8)`). A list group keeps its brackets: `P([x, x]) = x` / `Some = [P]:0` infers `Some([x])` and calls `P([x, x])` (`Some([7])` is `7`; `Some(7)` is TypeMismatch; `Some([7, 8])` ArityMismatch). A group left with no new binder contributes nothing. This follows the partial-group rule, not an exception for repeated names; a further formula forwards each surviving group as its own kind again (FWD-02). A callable alias is not inferred at all: `Some = P` is `P` itself by binding indirection, so `Some((7, 7))` is `7` and `Some(7)` is the kind mismatch of `P(7)` (re-run 2026-10-10, Phase A3, six routes; on 2026-09-29 the alias was a wrapper that inherited `P((x, x))` verbatim). (Before FWD-02's alias rule these observations belonged to `Some = P`; before the structural-pattern model the sequence group survived as the one-item `Some((x))`, whose one-level opening made `Some([7])` `7`, and PV-08 had rebuilt it as a list.) C# tests pin inference and these observations; Lean evaluates the corresponding explicit trees and does not prove signature inference.

- PAR-07 · constitution-draft.md:2711 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **Rule:** The front end rewrites some references in FORMULAS into synthesized calls (AUTOMATIC PARAMETER FORWARDING; the implementation and older records call it lifting). A non-root body whose ONE written row is a bare reference to a callable that declares parameters is not a formula: FWD-02 completes it as an exact alias or as bare forwarding by name, before this rule (decided 2026-09-29, finalized 2026-09-30). PAR-07 is the FORMULA rule: *inside an inferring formula, a bare reference to a parameterized callable may lift that callable's required parameter bindings into the containing inferred signature according to the by-name lifting rules below*; it is never the explanation of a closed body's lone row. Otherwise the rewrite applies when all three of the following hold:
  Now:
