- PAR-07 · constitution-draft.md:2712 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > - SIGNATURE: the reference RESOLVES — by the language's own order: the owner walk over the document's properties, then the prelude (builtins, the Math module and its aliases, the run's host operations; `load` has none), then the opens level by level, or a structural dot path to its member — to a callable whose LIFTING SIGNATURE REQUIRES supplied arguments (one an ordinary call supplying zero arguments cannot bind, CALL-05). The lifting signature is keyed by that identity (`ImplicitArgumentResolver.TryResolveLiftable`; Lean `Algorithm.liftingSignature?`): a user algorithm's processed parameter patterns (an exact alias's inherited ones included); a builtin's callable interface (`ToolingPlainSignature`: the registry's parameter names, a loop's `*init`); a Math member's or host operation's declared parameters; an opened or dotted member's own; and a CLAUSE FAMILY's one whole-value slot per position, named by the plain binders of its clauses (literal, structural and binderless patterns vote nothing; the votes must agree and the positions' names must be distinct; Lean `familyLiftingSignature?`). A family without such names has NO lifting signature and no name is invented: an INFERRING formula that would lift it is the front-end error `UnliftableClauseFamily`, while a closed level keeps its runtime zero-argument demand. A callable that accepts zero supplied arguments — no parameter, or only a top-level collector — is NEVER lifted, whatever its position: declaring a parameter does not by itself make a reference a call, so its bare name is the cached zero-argument value demand (CALL-05, PROP-04); a lone row naming it is an exact alias or bare forwarding instead (FWD-02).
  Now:
  > - SIGNATURE: the reference RESOLVES — by the language's own order: the owner walk over the document's properties, then the prelude (builtins, the Math module and its aliases, the run's host operations; `load` has none), then the opens level by level, or a structural dot path to its member — to a callable whose LIFTING SIGNATURE REQUIRES supplied arguments (one an ordinary call supplying zero arguments cannot bind, CALL-05). The lifting signature is keyed by that identity, resolved THROUGH callable aliases to their normalized target (`ImplicitArgumentResolver.TryResolveLiftable`; Lean `Algorithm.liftingSignature?`): a user algorithm's processed parameter patterns (a callable alias has none of its own: it lifts its target's, X-45); a builtin's callable interface (`ToolingPlainSignature`: the registry's parameter names, a loop's `*init`); a Math member's or host operation's declared parameters; an opened or dotted member's own; and a CLAUSE FAMILY's one whole-value slot per position, named by the plain binders of its clauses (literal, structural and binderless patterns vote nothing; the votes must agree and the positions' names must be distinct; Lean `familyLiftingSignature?`). A family without such names has NO lifting signature and no name is invented: an INFERRING formula that would lift it is the front-end error `UnliftableClauseFamily`, while a closed level keeps its runtime zero-argument demand. A callable that accepts zero supplied arguments — no parameter, or only a top-level collector — is NEVER lifted, whatever its position: declaring a parameter does not by itself make a reference a call, so its bare name is the cached zero-argument value demand (CALL-05, PROP-04); a lone row naming it is a callable alias or bare forwarding instead (FWD-02).

- PAR-07 · constitution-draft.md:2713 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > - ROLE: it appears where its immediate consumer demands its VALUE (`FormulaLiftingRoles`; Lean `liftingSlotRole`): an output row (other than the lone row FWD-02 completes) or deconstruction right-hand side, an operator or comparison operand, an index target or selector, a spread operand, a list or capture element, the `.string` receiver, a builtin's collection, value, whole-number or surplus slot (all three `if` slots; a loop's count and initial state), an argument of a Math member, a host operation or a clause family, or a slot of a selected dot fallback that is one of these (`R.F(args)` is `F(R, args)` slot by slot). The role is RECURSIVE — an expression nested in any slot takes its own consumer's role — and BLIND TO LAZINESS: an `if` branch lifts whether or not a run selects it (evaluation stays lazy).
  Now:
  > - ROLE: it appears in a VALUE-role position of its immediate consumer — a STATIC classification of the written position (`FormulaLiftingRoles`; Lean `liftingSlotRole`), never a run-time demand: an output row (other than the lone row FWD-02 completes) or deconstruction right-hand side, an operator or comparison operand, an index target or selector, a spread operand, a list or capture element, the `.string` receiver, a builtin's collection, value, whole-number or surplus slot (all three `if` slots; a loop's count and initial state), an argument of a Math member, a host operation or a clause family, or a slot of a selected dot fallback that is one of these (`R.F(args)` is `F(R, args)` slot by slot). The role is RECURSIVE — an expression nested in any slot takes its own consumer's role — and BLIND TO LAZINESS: an `if` branch lifts whether or not a run selects it. The role decides only the rewrite: the synthesized call is an ordinary supplied computation, demanded only when a consumer demands it at run time (NEED-01, NEED-05). So with `A = trace(x) + 1` and `Choose(0, a) = 0` / `Choose(n, a) = a`, `F = Choose(0, A)` / `F(5)` lifts `x` into `F` yet gives `0` with no trace, because the matching clause's plain binder `a` demands nothing (NEED-04), while `F = Choose(1, A)` / `F(5)` gives `6` and traces `5` once (re-run 2026-10-10, Phase A3, six routes). *(This bullet formerly said the immediate consumer "demands its VALUE", which since Model C, 2026-10-02, overstated the role: a clause family's plain binder, for one, demands nothing.)*

- PAR-07 · constitution-draft.md:2723 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **A forwarded parameter never changes a written name.** It is an ordinary parameter for every caller — arity, order, binding, activation, exposure — and a same-named property of its owner, or of a body nested in it, is still `ParameterPropertyCollision` (RES-05): `A = y + 1` / `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A + 0 }` / `F` → parseFailure `ParameterPropertyCollision` (`adv/h98` and `CALL-final/l01` observed it on the lone row `A`, which is now an exact alias whose inherited names are encapsulated: `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A }` / `F(5)` gives `6`, FWD-02). But it is never what a written identifier denotes. Name resolution decides every written name BEFORE forwarding, and nothing re-selects a binding afterwards. So adding a reference to a formula can never change what a previously resolvable identifier denotes, and extracting a sub-expression into a property keeps every binding the expression had.
  Now:
  > **A forwarded parameter never changes a written name.** It is an ordinary parameter for every caller — arity, order, binding, activation, exposure — and a same-named property of its owner, or of a body nested in it, is still `ParameterPropertyCollision` (RES-05): `A = y + 1` / `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A + 0 }` / `F` → parseFailure `ParameterPropertyCollision` (`adv/h98` and `CALL-final/l01` observed it on the lone row `A`, which is now a callable alias of `A`: it has no parameters of its own, and its own declaration `y = 3` never reaches the target's parameter, so `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A }` / `F(5)` gives `6`, FWD-02). But it is never what a written identifier denotes. Name resolution decides every written name BEFORE forwarding, and nothing re-selects a binding afterwards. So adding a reference to a formula can never change what a previously resolvable identifier denotes, and extracting a sub-expression into a property keeps every binding the expression had.

- PAR-07 · constitution-draft.md:2734 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **Formula forwarding is by binding name (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed; narrowed the same day to formulas by FWD-02's alias rule).** *Implicit forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns.* A caller owns ONE binding for a given parameter name. If a callee uses that name in several parameter positions — at the top level, inside a group, across groups, or beside a collector (`P(x, x)`, `P(x, y, x)`, `P((x, a), x)`, `P((x, y), (z, x))`, `P((x, *rest), x)`, `P(x, *rest, x)`, `P((x, x))`) — the forwarding source above is decided once for the NAME and supplied to every occurrence: `P(x, x) = x` / `D = P + 1` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly as `F(x)` / `G(x)` / `H = F + G` is `H(x) = F(x) + G(x)`. The language does not distinguish a name shared by two callees from a name used twice by one callee. One binding name is one caller parameter (PAR-05): `P(x, x, x)` lifts one `x`, `P((x, a), x)` lifts `(x, a)`, `P(x, (x, a))` lifts `x, a`, `P((x, x))` lifts `x` (a sequence group left with one binder IS that binder, PAR-05) — never `D(x, x)`, never one parameter per occurrence. A closed level that binds the name forwards its own binding into a formula (`Q(x) = P + 1` is `Q(x) = P(x, x) + 1`); one that does not follows PAR-04 (`Q(y) = P + 1` keeps `P` bare, and a strict Math position names the missing `x` once). Forwarding one binding to several occurrences manufactures nothing: each occurrence is an ordinary argument slot that receives that same complete binding — the value and callable of ONE argument, or its recorded failure (CALL-06) — so PAT-09's constraint over independently supplied arguments holds by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure, exactly as through the written `Same(x) = P(x, x)`. No lifting, neutral, closed or root position has a repeated-name case. A lone row is not a formula: `Some = P` is an exact alias inheriting `P(x, x)` — two independent arguments that must be equal — and `Q(x) = P` is bare forwarding, which reuses Q's one binding `x` by name for both occurrences, `P(x, x)` (FWD-02; the September 29 positional reading made it `P(x)`, P's own arity error). The alias deduplication this paragraph formerly stated (`Some = P` as `Some(x) = P(x, x)`) is superseded.
  Now:
  > **Formula forwarding is by binding name (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed; narrowed the same day to formulas by FWD-02's alias rule).** *Implicit forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns.* A caller owns ONE binding for a given parameter name. If a callee uses that name in several parameter positions — at the top level, inside a group, across groups, or beside a collector (`P(x, x)`, `P(x, y, x)`, `P((x, a), x)`, `P((x, y), (z, x))`, `P((x, *rest), x)`, `P(x, *rest, x)`, `P((x, x))`) — the forwarding source above is decided once for the NAME and supplied to every occurrence: `P(x, x) = x` / `D = P + 1` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly as `F(x)` / `G(x)` / `H = F + G` is `H(x) = F(x) + G(x)`. The language does not distinguish a name shared by two callees from a name used twice by one callee. One binding name is one caller parameter (PAR-05): `P(x, x, x)` lifts one `x`, `P((x, a), x)` lifts `(x, a)`, `P(x, (x, a))` lifts `x, a`, `P((x, x))` lifts `x` (a sequence group left with one binder IS that binder, PAR-05) — never `D(x, x)`, never one parameter per occurrence. A closed level that binds the name forwards its own binding into a formula (`Q(x) = P + 1` is `Q(x) = P(x, x) + 1`); one that does not follows PAR-04 (`Q(y) = P + 1` keeps `P` bare: when demanded it is the runtime `ArityMismatch`, in a strict Math position too — Q-15, decided 2026-10-02, removed the front-end report that formerly named the missing `x` once). Forwarding one binding to several occurrences manufactures nothing: each occurrence is an ordinary argument slot that receives that same complete binding — the ONE supplied cell, with its VALUE and CALLABLE channels and, once demanded, its completed failure (CALL-06, NEED-08) — so PAT-09's constraint over independently supplied arguments holds by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure, exactly as through the written `Same(x) = P(x, x)`. No lifting, neutral, closed or root position has a repeated-name case. A lone row is not a formula: `Some = P` is a callable alias whose CALLABLE identity is `P` itself by binding indirection (FWD-02, 2026-10-01), so a call through it supplies `P`'s two independent arguments, which must be equal — and `Q(x) = P` is bare forwarding, which reuses Q's one binding `x` by name for both occurrences, `P(x, x)` (FWD-02; the September 29 positional reading made it `P(x)`, P's own arity error). The alias deduplication this paragraph formerly stated (`Some = P` as `Some(x) = P(x, x)`) is superseded, and so is the wrapper reading of 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01, under which the alias inherited `P(x, x)` as a signature of its own.

- PAR-07 · constitution-draft.md:2736 · Why fundamental (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **Why fundamental:** It is how formulas compose ("formulas that use formulas"). `KineticEnergy = mass * Speed ^ 2 / 2` takes `Speed`'s inputs. It also means callee parameter names are observable in formulas, because formula forwarding is by name — deliberately (Q-74, resolved 2026-09-30 as the distinction between formula lifting, bare forwarding and explicit calls): one binding name is one input, however many times the callees use it, so a name shared by two callees and a name repeated within one callee are the same case. Neutral argument positions are what keep `Twice(A)` a higher-order use of `A` rather than a call. Because forwarding only ever reuses what a written reference already denotes, a helper extracted from an expression means exactly the inlined expression, and an unrelated declaration elsewhere can never change a formula's signature. A lone row names a callable rather than using it, so it is an exact alias or bare forwarding (FWD-02): the alias infers nothing, and bare forwarding reuses existing bindings by name but never adds one to a closed list.
  Now:
  > **Why fundamental:** It is how formulas compose ("formulas that use formulas"). `KineticEnergy = mass * Speed ^ 2 / 2` takes `Speed`'s inputs. It also means callee parameter names are observable in formulas, because formula forwarding is by name — deliberately (Q-74, resolved 2026-09-30 as the distinction between formula lifting, bare forwarding and explicit calls): one binding name is one input, however many times the callees use it, so a name shared by two callees and a name repeated within one callee are the same case. Neutral argument positions are what keep `Twice(A)` a higher-order use of `A` rather than a call. Because forwarding only ever reuses what a written reference already denotes, a helper extracted from an expression means exactly the inlined expression, and an unrelated declaration elsewhere can never change a formula's signature. A lone row names a callable rather than using it, so it is a callable alias or bare forwarding (FWD-02): the alias infers nothing, and bare forwarding reuses existing bindings by name but never adds one to a closed list.

  > - Who supplies the occurrences decides what is checked, with `Common(x, x) = x` (spec `repeated-name-wrapper-keeps-independent-arguments`): `Twice(v) = Common(v, v)` supplies one binding to both occurrences (`Twice(8)` gives `8`), while `Both(a, b) = Common(a, b)` and the callable alias `Some = Common` (which IS `Common`) keep two independently supplied arguments (`Both(7, 8)` fails as `Common(7, 8)` does, and `Some(9, 9)` gives `9`; by binding name `Some(9)` gave `9`). `F(x) = x + 1` / `G(x) = x * 2` / `H = F + G` / `H(3)` gives `10`.

- FWD-01 · constitution-draft.md:3375 · title (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > ### FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S

- FWD-01 · constitution-draft.md:3379 · Rule (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > **Rule:** For every supply `S`, spreading the list that a collector built from `S` re-supplies exactly `S`. So `Forward(*items) = Target(items*)`, or equivalently `items*.Target`, hands `Target` the same items, in the same order, that `Forward` received. This includes zero items, `()`, `[]` and nested structures, and a collecting `Target` re-collects an equal list.
  Now:
  > **Rule:** For every supply `S`, re-spreading the collector bound to `S` re-supplies exactly `S`. So `Forward(*items) = Target(items*)`, or equivalently `items*.Target`, hands `Target` the same items, in the same order, that `Forward` received — the same supplied cells, each with its VALUE computation and any CALLABLE identity it was supplied with, and the transfer demands none of them (VAR-03, NEED-07, NEED-08). This includes zero items, `()`, `[]` and nested structures, and a collecting `Target` re-collects an equal list. At the value level, reading the collector materializes one exact list (VAR-01) whose spread supplies the values of `S`: spread(collect(S)) = S.

- FWD-01 · constitution-draft.md:3381 · Rule (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > - Passing the collected list WITHOUT the spread passes ONE list argument. A collector then collects `[items]`, and a fixed parameter binds the list.
  Now:
  > - Passing the collector WITHOUT the spread passes ONE argument: the collector's own cell, one collection-valued computation, transported undemanded (NEED-08). A collector then collects it as the one item of `[items]`, and a fixed parameter binds it; its VALUE, when demanded, is the exact list, and a later `v*` of that fixed parameter still re-spreads the original cells (VAR-03).

- FWD-01 · constitution-draft.md:3383 · Rule (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > - A reference to a collected binding is just an ordinary list value. Forwarding carries no runtime supply provenance (VAR-04).
  Now:
  > - Read as a value, a collected binding is an ordinary exact list: the read materializes every cell left to right, and the first failing cell is the read's failure (VAR-03, NEED-07). Forwarding carries no runtime supply provenance beyond the transferred cells themselves (VAR-04).

- FWD-01 · constitution-draft.md:3397 · Normal example (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > - `Coll(L*) == L` with `L = [1, 2]` → `true`.
  Now:
  > - `Coll(L*) == L` with `L = [1, 2]` → `true`.
  > - Re-spreading transfers cells without demanding them and keeps their callables: `Target(*xs) = 0` / `Forward(*items) = Target(items*)` / `Forward(trace(1), trace(2))` → `0` with an empty host log; `Inc(x) = x + 1` / `Apply(f) = f(9)` / `Fwd(*fs) = Apply(fs*)` / `Fwd(Inc)` → `10`, and so does the collector carried through a fixed parameter (`Inner(v) = Apply(v*)` / `Outer(*fs) = Inner(fs)` / `Outer(Inc)` → `10`); `ForwardOne(*items) = Target(items)` with `Target(*xs) = 0` and `ForwardOne(trace(1))` → `0`, no host event. A demanded read stops at its first failing cell: `Target(*xs) = xs` / `Forward(trace(1), trace(1) / 0, trace(3))` is `DivisionByZero` after `[trace(1), trace(1)]` (re-run 2026-10-10, Phase A3, six routes; Lean agrees on the derived programs that reach no host operation).

- FWD-02 · constitution-draft.md:3460 · Rule (under: FWD-02 — An alias preserves the callable it names, bare forwarding reuses existing compati)
  >   Unused parameters of the body stay unused. A row that forwards nothing (every callee parameter an unsupplied collector) is the bare name — CALL-05's cached read, never an invented call.   Now:
  >   Unused parameters of the body stay unused. A row that forwards nothing (every callee parameter an unsupplied collector) is the bare name — CALL-05's cached read, never an invented call. Forwarding transports cells and demands none of them (NEED-08).

- FWD-02 · constitution-draft.md:3463 · Rule (under: FWD-02 — An alias preserves the callable it names, bare forwarding reuses existing compati)
  > - *Every synthesized call — bare forwarding or a formula's lifted call (PAR-07); an alias synthesizes none — forwards existing bindings unchanged and rebuilds each structural pattern as its own kind.* A fixed binding is supplied as its whole value, never opened and never wrapped; a collecting binding is re-spread as exactly its collected items — in bare forwarding and a formula only when BOTH the destination capture and the source binding collect (the source binding is the one this rule or PAR-07 selects, a reused enclosing binding included; its kind decides), so an ordinary parameter is never re-spread into a collecting destination and a collected list forwarded into a fixed destination stays one list argument. A reconstructed sequence pattern is a sequence (the capture of its items; `()` for none; its one lone non-spread item itself, because the written `C((xs))` IS `C(xs)` and a one-item sequence pattern does not exist, PAT-06) and a reconstructed list pattern a list (the list literal of its items), at every nesting level. No forwarding step converts between sequence and list kinds. Consequently every synthesized call is exactly the call a programmer would write.
  Now:
  > - *Every synthesized call — bare forwarding or a formula's lifted call (PAR-07); an alias synthesizes none — forwards existing bindings unchanged and rebuilds each structural pattern as its own kind.* A fixed binding is supplied whole — its one cell, VALUE and CALLABLE channels intact and undemanded (NEED-08) — never opened and never wrapped; a collecting binding is re-spread as exactly its collected cells — in bare forwarding and a formula only when BOTH the destination capture and the source binding collect (the source binding is the one this rule or PAR-07 selects, a reused enclosing binding included; its kind decides), so an ordinary parameter is never re-spread into a collecting destination and a collector forwarded into a fixed destination stays one argument (the collector's own cell, one collection-valued computation). A reconstructed sequence pattern is a sequence (the capture of its items; `()` for none; its one lone non-spread item itself, because the written `C((xs))` IS `C(xs)` and a one-item sequence pattern does not exist, PAT-06) and a reconstructed list pattern a list (the list literal of its items), at every nesting level. No forwarding step converts between sequence and list kinds. Consequently every synthesized call is exactly the call a programmer would write.

  > - Alias targets (decided 2026-10-01, binding indirection): every identity that declares parameterized callable structure — every builtin, through its own adapter (`I = if` / `I(true, 1, 1 / 0)` is `1`; `M = map` / `M([], Eff)` never evaluates `Eff`; `C = count` / `C(1 / 0, 2)` keeps count's `ArityMismatch`; `R = repeat` keeps its at-least-three minimum), every clause family, nameable or not, through its own dispatch (`F = Fact` / `F(1, 2)` is `NoMatchingBranch`; `A = U` with an unnameable `U` is an alias), and every user algorithm with a parameter, on every route.   Now:

Not targets: a zero-parameter identity (the row reads it), a callable parameter, an unresolved name and an ambiguous open name (no identity). BARE FORWARDING still needs a forwarding contract: an unnameable family has none, so a closed lone row naming one — directly or through an alias — is the front-end error `UnforwardableCallable` (Q-77, decided 2026-10-01). *History:* until X-47 was implemented (2026-10-01) the C# front end applied the route-based eligibility and the wrapper (`C = count`, `AliasG = G`, `A = trace`, `A = Lib.X` and `open Math` / `A = Abs` were zero-parameter properties; a lexical user alias was a wrapper). *History:* the callable-capability rule (2026-10-01, earlier the same day) excluded builtins and families from aliases because a delegating WRAPPER changes their invocation (a delegating `A = if` made `A(true, 1, 1 / 0)` `DivisionByZero`, `count(1 / 0, 2)`'s `ArityMismatch` became `DivisionByZero`, an alias through a family's clause-named signature turned `NoMatchingBranch` into `ArityMismatch`); binding indirection has no wrapper, so the exclusion has no basis.

This held for ordinary failures; a resource limit ends the run in both spellings (RUN-03, since the Q-02 decision of 2026-09-28). *(Historical: resolved by Model C, 2026-10-02 — a supplied argument is demanded only when used, so `K(1.Div), K(Div(1))` is `5, 5` and `K(f) = f + 1` / `K(1.Div)` traces once.)*

- RES-05 · constitution-draft.md:4462 · Rule (under: RES-05 — A property may not share a name with a parameter of its own or of any enclosing o)
  > - **Alias exemption (FWD-02, decided 2026-09-29).** An exact alias's inherited signature is not checked at all: its names are the callee's private binder names, owned by no written name, so a property of the alias or of a body nested in it may share one (`F(x) = x + 1` / `A = { x = 100 ⏎ F }` / `A(5)` → `6`: the synthesized call reads the inherited parameter, never the property). A formula's forwarded parameter still counts.
  Now:
  > - **No alias exemption is needed (FWD-02; binding indirection since 2026-10-01).** A callable alias has no parameters of its own, so nothing about it can collide: a property of the alias or of a body nested in it may share a name with a parameter of its target (`F(x) = x + 1` / `A = { x = 100 ⏎ F }` / `A(5)` → `6`: the call is the target's own, whose parameter `x` the alias's property never reaches; re-run 2026-10-10, Phase A3, six routes). A formula's forwarded parameter still counts. *(From 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01 this was the "alias exemption": the wrapper alias inherited its callee's signature, which the collision check skipped — `Algorithm.User.InheritsCalleeSignature` and its `ParameterPropertyCollisionValidator` exemption, deleted with the wrapper.)*

- PAT-03 · constitution-draft.md:8678 · Rule (under: PAT-03 — A family has one outer call interface: every clause takes the same number of argu)
  > - **(b) Exact slot count.** A head of arity n matches only a call supplying exactly n argument slots. Each top-level pattern consumes exactly one slot. Surplus arguments are never dropped and missing ones never defaulted, so a wrong argument count selects no clause (NoMatchingBranch). Arity therefore never distinguishes clauses.
  Now:
  > - **(b) Exact slot count.** A head of arity n matches only a call supplying exactly n argument slots. Each top-level pattern consumes exactly one slot. Surplus arguments are never dropped and missing ones never defaulted, so a wrong argument count selects no clause: the call's cardinality is rejected as `ArityMismatch` before any clause is tried or any argument demanded (NEED-05; until Model C, 2026-10-02, it was `NoMatchingBranch`). Arity therefore never distinguishes clauses.

  >   - A clause family reports the wrong count as `NoMatchingBranch`: `Fam(0) = 0` / `Fam(n) = n` / `Fam(1, 2)` (too many, `f13a.kat`) and `Fam(0, y) = 0` / `Fam(n, y) = n` / `Fam(5)` (too few, `f13b.kat`) are both `err NoMatchingBranch` on all five paths (also adversarial probes `h93`, `h95`).

- RUN-03 · constitution-draft.md:10768 · Rule (under: RUN-03 — Runtime protection is host policy: it may stop a run, never redefine it)
  > - **Never postponed or absorbed.** No construct can defer, absorb or replace it: not a binding that is never read afterwards, a supplied computation's memo (a reached limit is never a cell's completed outcome, NEED-02), forwarding, a builtin's arity verdict, an earlier ordinary failure, or a consumer's choice. A resource limit is therefore never a slot's recorded outcome (CALL-06). What separates it from an ORDINARY failure: an ordinary failure becomes the completed outcome of the computation that raised it (NEED-02, CALL-06), and a reached limit never does. Both end the run once evaluation that actually occurs raises them, and a supplied computation that is never demanded runs nothing and reaches neither (RUN-08).
  Now:
  > - **Never postponed or absorbed.** No construct can defer, absorb or replace it: not a binding that is never read afterwards, a supplied computation's memo, forwarding, a builtin's arity verdict, an earlier ordinary failure, or a consumer's choice. A demanded cell that reaches a limit stores it as its TERMINAL completion, and the run's budget retains that error, so the cell never restarts and no later semantic work — no further evaluation, memo read, CALLABLE projection, random draw or host operation — runs (NEED-02, NEED-09; C# `NeedCell.Complete` with `EvaluationBudget.RetainTerminal` / `CheckContinuation`). What separates it from an ORDINARY failure: an ordinary failure is the completed outcome of the computation that raised it (NEED-02, CALL-06) and fails only the demands that reach it, while a reached limit is terminal for the whole run; neither is ever a recoverable argument value or a clause mismatch, and neither enters the success-only property cache (NEED-10). *(Phase A3, 2026-10-10: until then this bullet said that "a reached limit is never a cell's completed outcome" and "never a slot's recorded outcome", contradicting `NeedCell.Complete`, NEED-02's "stored terminal completion" and CALL-06 as corrected by the A2 independent review.)* Both end the run once evaluation that actually occurs raises them, and a supplied computation that is never demanded runs nothing and reaches neither (RUN-08).

- RUN topic · constitution-draft.md:11328 · Deliberately non-constitutional (under: Deliberately non-constitutional in this topic)
  > - **Operational counters and step granularity.** Planned loops charge fewer steps (probed 20 vs 23, 13 vs 16, 27 vs 32). Peak depth and plan or fusion hits are also counters. They are unobservable as verdicts because configured step, string or materialization budgets force the generic strategies.
  Now:
  > - **Operational counters.** Peak depth and plan or fusion hits are observations, not semantics. Every strategy charges every semantic budget identically at the same logical points, and no configured limit selects a strategy (RUN-03, Q-09b, decided 2026-10-04). *(Until 2026-10-04 this entry read: "Planned loops charge fewer steps (probed 20 vs 23, 13 vs 16, 27 vs 32). … They are unobservable as verdicts because configured step, string or materialization budgets force the generic strategies." — PV-07, resolved.)*

- RUN topic · constitution-draft.md:11343 · Deliberately non-constitutional (under: Deliberately non-constitutional in this topic)
  > - **How terminality is implemented.** `Evaluator.IsDeferrableEvaluationFailure` is consulted by user-call assembly, the builtin adapter and the fused filter-count pipeline, and the adapter keeps consumer-side backstops. Only RUN-03's law is constitutional. (Until the Q-02 decision of 2026-09-28 this entry was the sticky retention of resource-limit argument failures, `RetainResourceLimitForAlgorithmBinding`: limit policy against exponential retry, whose semantic leak was the RUN-03 tension. It is deleted.)
  Now:
  > - **How terminality is implemented:** `NeedCell.Complete` stores a demanded resource failure as the cell's terminal completion and `EvaluationBudget.RetainTerminal` / `CheckContinuation` stop later work (RUN-03, NEED-09). `Evaluator.IsDeferrableEvaluationFailure` survives only as builtin demand-report precedence through `SequenceBuiltinValueDemandError`. Only RUN-03's law is constitutional. *Historical:* until Model C (2026-10-02) the predicate was consulted by user-call assembly (`BuildCallArgumentInputs`), the builtin adapter's eager item attempt and the fused filter-count pipeline, and the adapter kept consumer-side backstops; until the Q-02 decision of 2026-09-28 this entry was the sticky retention of resource-limit argument failures, `RetainResourceLimitForAlgorithmBinding` — limit policy against exponential retry, whose semantic leak was the RUN-03 tension (deleted).

- CALL-01 · constitution-summary.md:462 · Rule (under: CALL-01 — A call selects one callee identity first and binds against that callee's signatu)
  > - A supply that the selected signature cannot bind is an evaluation-time error: `ArityMismatch` for a user or builtin callee, and `NoMatchingBranch` for a clause family, where a wrong argument count selects no clause (see PAT-03(b)). It is never a parse-time error, and an unevaluated wrong-arity call is inert.
  Now:
  > - A supply that the selected signature cannot bind is an evaluation-time error: `ArityMismatch` for every callee category whose cardinality the supply misses — a user or builtin callee, and a clause family, whose wrong argument count no clause head accepts (NEED-05; see PAT-03(b)) — and `NoMatchingBranch` for a clause family supplied an accepted count that no clause matches (PAT-02). *(Until Model C, 2026-10-02, a family's wrong count was `NoMatchingBranch` too.)* It is never a parse-time error, and an unevaluated wrong-arity call is inert.

- CALL-04 · constitution-summary.md:498 · Rule (under: CALL-04 — Arity counts supplied items, and a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged in e)
  > - A parameter list is satisfied by the number of supplied ITEMS, never by the element count of any value.
  Now:
  > - A parameter list is satisfied by the number of supplied ITEMS, never by the element count of any value. The supplied items are the call's supply cells (CALL-02): one per non-spread written slot, whatever its kind or eventual VALUE, and one per item an explicit spread opens (NEED-01, NEED-07).

- CALL-04 · constitution-summary.md:499 · Rule (under: CALL-04 — Arity counts supplied items, and a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged in e)
  > - A fixed parameter binds exactly one supplied item, unchanged, whatever its kind: a sequence, a list, `()` or `[]` stays one value.
  Now:
  > - A fixed parameter binds exactly one supplied item, unchanged, whatever its kind: a sequence, a list, `()` or `[]` stays one value. Binding attaches the item's cell without demanding it; when that VALUE is demanded it is the item's value, unchanged (NEED-01, NEED-04).

- CALL-04 · constitution-summary.md:501 · Rule (under: CALL-04 — Arity counts supplied items, and a fixed parameter binds its item unchanged in e)
  > - A supplied count that the flat signature does not accept is `ArityMismatch`. This holds identically for the direct call `F(v)`, the dotted call `v.F` (see DOT), and a callback (see ALGHO). A failed spread supplies no item, so it never takes part in an arity verdict: its own failure is raised first (SUP-02).
  Now:
  > - A supplied count that the selected callee does not accept is `ArityMismatch`, raised before any non-spread supplied computation is demanded (NEED-05). This holds identically for the direct call `F(v)`, the dotted call `v.F` (see DOT), a callback (see ALGHO) and every callee category, a clause family included: a family rejects a count no clause head accepts as `ArityMismatch` before trying any clause, and reports `NoMatchingBranch` only for an accepted count that no clause matches (PAT-02, PAT-03). A failed spread supplies no item, so it never takes part in an arity verdict: its own failure is raised first (SUP-02).

- PAR-04 · constitution-summary.md:570 · Rule (under: PAR-04 — An explicit parameter list is closed for its own level: nothing is inferred there)

- PAR-05 · constitution-summary.md:585 · Rule (under: PAR-05 — An inferred signature lists the level's own names by first semantic occurrence, f)
  > Own names and lifted names are never interleaved. The order in which a runtime fallback assembles its call never determines the signature order. An exact alias (FWD-02) infers nothing: it inherits its callee's parameter patterns verbatim, and bare forwarding keeps its written list. A destination callable's parameter order never reorders an explicit source list.
  Now:
  > Own names and lifted names are never interleaved. The order in which a runtime fallback assembles its call never determines the signature order. A callable alias (FWD-02) infers nothing: it has no signature of its own — its CALLABLE identity is its target's, by binding indirection (2026-10-01) — and bare forwarding keeps its written list. A destination callable's parameter order never reorders an explicit source list.

- PAR-07 · constitution-summary.md:619 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **Rule:** The front end rewrites some references in FORMULAS into synthesized calls (AUTOMATIC PARAMETER FORWARDING; the implementation and older records call it lifting). A non-root body whose ONE written row is a bare reference to a callable that declares parameters is not a formula: FWD-02 completes it as an exact alias or as bare forwarding by name, before this rule (decided 2026-09-29, finalized 2026-09-30). PAR-07 is the FORMULA rule: *inside an inferring formula, a bare reference to a parameterized callable may lift that callable's required parameter bindings into the containing inferred signature according to the by-name lifting rules below*; it is never the explanation of a closed body's lone row. Otherwise the rewrite applies when all three of the following hold:
  Now:
  > **Rule:** The front end rewrites some references in FORMULAS into synthesized calls (AUTOMATIC PARAMETER FORWARDING; the implementation and older records call it lifting). A non-root body whose ONE written row is a bare reference to a callable that declares parameters is not a formula: FWD-02 completes it as a callable alias (binding indirection) or as bare forwarding by name, before this rule (decided 2026-09-29, finalized 2026-09-30). PAR-07 is the FORMULA rule: *inside an inferring formula, a bare reference to a parameterized callable may lift that callable's required parameter bindings into the containing inferred signature according to the by-name lifting rules below*; it is never the explanation of a closed body's lone row. Otherwise the rewrite applies when all three of the following hold:

- PAR-07 · constitution-summary.md:620 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > - SIGNATURE: the reference resolves (owner walk, then the prelude, then the opens, or a structural dot path) to a callable whose identity-keyed LIFTING SIGNATURE requires supplied arguments (CALL-05) — a user algorithm, a builtin (`ToolingPlainSignature`), a Math member, a host operation, an opened or dotted member, or a clause family named by its clauses' plain binders (else `UnliftableClauseFamily` in an inferring formula; no name is ever invented). A callable that accepts zero supplied arguments — no parameter, or only a top-level collector — is NEVER lifted, whatever its position: declaring a parameter does not by itself make a reference a call, so its bare name is the cached zero-argument value demand (CALL-05, PROP-04); a lone row naming it is an exact alias or bare forwarding instead (FWD-02).
  Now:
  > - SIGNATURE: the reference resolves (owner walk, then the prelude, then the opens, or a structural dot path) to a callable whose identity-keyed LIFTING SIGNATURE — resolved through callable aliases to their normalized target — requires supplied arguments (CALL-05) — a user algorithm, a builtin (`ToolingPlainSignature`), a Math member, a host operation, an opened or dotted member, or a clause family named by its clauses' plain binders (else `UnliftableClauseFamily` in an inferring formula; no name is ever invented). A callable that accepts zero supplied arguments — no parameter, or only a top-level collector — is NEVER lifted, whatever its position: declaring a parameter does not by itself make a reference a call, so its bare name is the cached zero-argument value demand (CALL-05, PROP-04); a lone row naming it is a callable alias or bare forwarding instead (FWD-02).

- PAR-07 · constitution-summary.md:621 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > - ROLE: its immediate consumer demands its VALUE (`FormulaLiftingRoles`): an output row (other than the lone row FWD-02 completes) or deconstruction right-hand side, an operator or comparison operand, an index target or selector, a spread operand, a list or capture element, the `.string` receiver, a builtin's collection, value, whole-number or surplus slot, an argument of a Math member, a host operation or a clause family, or a slot of a selected dot fallback that is one of these — recursively through any enclosing slot, and blind to laziness (a callee, a callback or loop step, a user callable's whole argument, a runtime-only callee's argument and a navigated receiver keep the reference).
  Now:
  > - ROLE: it appears in a VALUE-role position of its immediate consumer — a STATIC classification of the written position (`FormulaLiftingRoles`), never a run-time demand: an output row (other than the lone row FWD-02 completes) or deconstruction right-hand side, an operator or comparison operand, an index target or selector, a spread operand, a list or capture element, the `.string` receiver, a builtin's collection, value, whole-number or surplus slot, an argument of a Math member, a host operation or a clause family, or a slot of a selected dot fallback that is one of these — recursively through any enclosing slot, and blind to laziness (a callee, a callback or loop step, a user callable's whole argument, a runtime-only callee's argument and a navigated receiver keep the reference). The role decides only the rewrite: the synthesized call is an ordinary supplied computation, demanded only when a consumer demands it at run time (NEED-01, NEED-05) — with `Choose(0, a) = 0` / `Choose(n, a) = a`, `F = Choose(0, A)` lifts `A`'s parameter into `F`, yet a call of `F` that selects the first clause never evaluates `A` (NEED-04).

- PAR-07 · constitution-summary.md:631 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **Formula forwarding is by binding name (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed; narrowed the same day to formulas by FWD-02's alias rule).** *Implicit forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns.* A caller owns ONE binding for a given parameter name; if a callee uses that name in several parameter positions (at the top level, inside a group, across groups, beside a collector), the forwarding source is decided once for the NAME and supplied to every occurrence: `P(x, x) = x` / `D = P + 1` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly as `H = F + G` with `F(x)` and `G(x)` is `H(x) = F(x) + G(x)`. One binding name is one caller parameter (PAR-05), never one per occurrence. A closed level that binds the name forwards its own binding into a formula (`Q(x) = P + 1` is `Q(x) = P(x, x) + 1`); one that does not follows PAR-04. Each occurrence receives the same complete binding, so nothing is merged (PAT-09). A lone row is not a formula: `Some = P` is an exact alias with P's two independent arguments, and `Q(x) = P` is bare forwarding, which reuses Q's one binding `x` by name for both occurrences, `P(x, x)` (FWD-02).
  Now:
  > **Formula forwarding is by binding name (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed; narrowed the same day to formulas by FWD-02's alias rule).** *Implicit forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns.* A caller owns ONE binding for a given parameter name; if a callee uses that name in several parameter positions (at the top level, inside a group, across groups, beside a collector), the forwarding source is decided once for the NAME and supplied to every occurrence: `P(x, x) = x` / `D = P + 1` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly as `H = F + G` with `F(x)` and `G(x)` is `H(x) = F(x) + G(x)`. One binding name is one caller parameter (PAR-05), never one per occurrence. A closed level that binds the name forwards its own binding into a formula (`Q(x) = P + 1` is `Q(x) = P(x, x) + 1`); one that does not follows PAR-04. Each occurrence receives the same complete binding — the one supplied cell (NEED-08) — so nothing is merged (PAT-09). A lone row is not a formula: `Some = P` is a callable alias — `P` itself by binding indirection, so a call through it supplies P's two independent arguments — and `Q(x) = P` is bare forwarding, which reuses Q's one binding `x` by name for both occurrences, `P(x, x)` (FWD-02).

- PAR-07 · constitution-summary.md:633 · Rule (under: PAR-07 — In a formula, a value-role reference to a callable that requires supplied argumen)
  > **A forwarded parameter never changes a written name.** It is an ordinary parameter for every caller — arity, order, binding, activation, exposure — and a same-named property of its owner, or of a body nested in it, is still `ParameterPropertyCollision` (RES-05): `A = y + 1` / `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A + 0 }` / `F` → parseFailure `ParameterPropertyCollision` (`adv/h98` and `CALL-final/l01` observed it on the lone row `A`, which is now an exact alias whose inherited names are encapsulated: `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A }` / `F(5)` gives `6`, FWD-02). But it is never what a written identifier denotes. Name resolution decides every written name BEFORE forwarding, and nothing re-selects a binding afterwards. So adding a reference to a formula can never change what a previously resolvable identifier denotes, and extracting a sub-expression into a property keeps every binding the expression had.
  Now:
  > **A forwarded parameter never changes a written name.** It is an ordinary parameter for every caller — arity, order, binding, activation, exposure — and a same-named property of its owner, or of a body nested in it, is still `ParameterPropertyCollision` (RES-05): `A = y + 1` / `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A + 0 }` / `F` → parseFailure `ParameterPropertyCollision` (`adv/h98` and `CALL-final/l01` observed it on the lone row `A`, which is now a callable alias of `A`: it has no parameters of its own, and its own declaration `y = 3` never reaches the target's parameter, so `F = { y = 3 ⏎ A }` / `F(5)` gives `6`, FWD-02). But it is never what a written identifier denotes. Name resolution decides every written name BEFORE forwarding, and nothing re-selects a binding afterwards. So adding a reference to a formula can never change what a previously resolvable identifier denotes, and extracting a sub-expression into a property keeps every binding the expression had.

- FWD-01 · constitution-summary.md:750 · title (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > ### FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S

- FWD-01 · constitution-summary.md:754 · Rule (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > **Rule:** For every supply `S`, spreading the list that a collector built from `S` re-supplies exactly `S`. So `Forward(*items) = Target(items*)`, or equivalently `items*.Target`, hands `Target` the same items, in the same order, that `Forward` received. This includes zero items, `()`, `[]` and nested structures, and a collecting `Target` re-collects an equal list.
  Now:
  > **Rule:** For every supply `S`, re-spreading the collector bound to `S` re-supplies exactly `S`. So `Forward(*items) = Target(items*)`, or equivalently `items*.Target`, hands `Target` the same items, in the same order, that `Forward` received — the same supplied cells, each with its VALUE computation and any CALLABLE identity it was supplied with, and the transfer demands none of them (VAR-03, NEED-07, NEED-08). This includes zero items, `()`, `[]` and nested structures, and a collecting `Target` re-collects an equal list. At the value level, reading the collector materializes one exact list (VAR-01) whose spread supplies the values of `S`: spread(collect(S)) = S.

- FWD-01 · constitution-summary.md:756 · Rule (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > - Passing the collected list WITHOUT the spread passes ONE list argument. A collector then collects `[items]`, and a fixed parameter binds the list.
  Now:
  > - Passing the collector WITHOUT the spread passes ONE argument: the collector's own cell, one collection-valued computation, transported undemanded (NEED-08). A collector then collects it as the one item of `[items]`, and a fixed parameter binds it; its VALUE, when demanded, is the exact list, and a later `v*` of that fixed parameter still re-spreads the original cells (VAR-03).

- FWD-01 · constitution-summary.md:758 · Rule (under: FWD-01 — Forwarding collected arguments is ordinary list spread: spread(collect(S)) = S)
  > - A reference to a collected binding is just an ordinary list value. Forwarding carries no runtime supply provenance (VAR-04).
  Now:
  > - Read as a value, a collected binding is an ordinary exact list: the read materializes every cell left to right, and the first failing cell is the read's failure (VAR-03, NEED-07). Forwarding carries no runtime supply provenance beyond the transferred cells themselves (VAR-04).

- FWD-02 · constitution-summary.md:782 · Rule (under: FWD-02 — An alias preserves the callable it names, bare forwarding reuses existing compati)
  >   Unused parameters of the body stay unused. A row that forwards nothing (every callee parameter an unsupplied collector) is the bare name — CALL-05's cached read, never an invented call. Binding kind is preserved by FWD-01's source-kind rule: a collecting source re-spreads only into a collecting destination; every other pair passes the binding whole.
  Now:
  >   Unused parameters of the body stay unused. A row that forwards nothing (every callee parameter an unsupplied collector) is the bare name — CALL-05's cached read, never an invented call. Binding kind is preserved by FWD-01's source-kind rule: a collecting source re-spreads its collected cells only into a collecting destination; every other pair passes the binding whole, as its one cell. Forwarding transports cells and demands none of them (NEED-08).

- FWD-02 · constitution-summary.md:785 · Rule (under: FWD-02 — An alias preserves the callable it names, bare forwarding reuses existing compati)
  > - *Every synthesized call — bare forwarding or a formula's lifted call (PAR-07); an alias synthesizes none — forwards existing bindings unchanged and rebuilds each structural pattern as its own kind.* A fixed binding is supplied as its whole value, never opened and never wrapped; a collecting binding is re-spread as exactly its collected items — in bare forwarding and a formula only when BOTH the destination capture and the source binding collect (the source binding is the one this rule or PAR-07 selects, a reused enclosing binding included; its kind decides), so an ordinary parameter is never re-spread into a collecting destination and a collected list forwarded into a fixed destination stays one list argument. A reconstructed sequence pattern is a sequence (the capture of its items; `()` for none; its one lone non-spread item itself, because the written `C((xs))` IS `C(xs)` and a one-item sequence pattern does not exist, PAT-06) and a reconstructed list pattern a list (the list literal of its items), at every nesting level. No forwarding step converts between sequence and list kinds. Consequently every synthesized call is exactly the call a programmer would write.
  Now:
  > - *Every synthesized call — bare forwarding or a formula's lifted call (PAR-07); an alias synthesizes none — forwards existing bindings unchanged and rebuilds each structural pattern as its own kind.* A fixed binding is supplied whole — its one cell, VALUE and CALLABLE channels intact and undemanded (NEED-08) — never opened and never wrapped; a collecting binding is re-spread as exactly its collected cells — in bare forwarding and a formula only when BOTH the destination capture and the source binding collect (the source binding is the one this rule or PAR-07 selects, a reused enclosing binding included; its kind decides), so an ordinary parameter is never re-spread into a collecting destination and a collector forwarded into a fixed destination stays one argument (the collector's own cell, one collection-valued computation). A reconstructed sequence pattern is a sequence (the capture of its items; `()` for none; its one lone non-spread item itself, because the written `C((xs))` IS `C(xs)` and a one-item sequence pattern does not exist, PAT-06) and a reconstructed list pattern a list (the list literal of its items), at every nesting level. No forwarding step converts between sequence and list kinds. Consequently every synthesized call is exactly the call a programmer would write.

- RES-05 · constitution-summary.md:981 · Rule (under: RES-05 — A property may not share a name with a parameter of its own or of any enclosing o)
  > - **Alias exemption (FWD-02, decided 2026-09-29).** An exact alias's inherited signature is not checked at all: its names are the callee's private binder names, owned by no written name, so a property of the alias or of a body nested in it may share one (`F(x) = x + 1` / `A = { x = 100 ⏎ F }` / `A(5)` → `6`: the synthesized call reads the inherited parameter, never the property). A formula's forwarded parameter still counts.
  Now:
  > - **No alias exemption is needed (FWD-02; binding indirection since 2026-10-01).** A callable alias has no parameters of its own, so nothing about it can collide: a property of the alias or of a body nested in it may share a name with a parameter of its target (`F(x) = x + 1` / `A = { x = 100 ⏎ F }` / `A(5)` → `6`: the call is the target's own, whose parameter `x` the alias's property never reaches; re-run 2026-10-10, Phase A3, six routes). A formula's forwarded parameter still counts. *(From 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-01 this was the "alias exemption": the wrapper alias inherited its callee's signature, which the collision check skipped — `Algorithm.User.InheritsCalleeSignature` and its `ParameterPropertyCollisionValidator` exemption, deleted with the wrapper.)*

- PAT-02 · constitution-summary.md:1912 · Rule (under: PAT-02 — A family call selects the first matching clause in written order; no match is NoM)
  > - **No match.** If no clause matches, the call fails with NoMatchingBranch. It never fails with ArityMismatch and never yields a default value.
  Now:
  > - **No match.** If no clause matches a supply of an accepted count, the call fails with NoMatchingBranch; it never yields a default value. A count no clause head accepts is rejected before any clause is tried, as the call's cardinality `ArityMismatch` (NEED-05; PAT-03(b)). *(Until Model C, 2026-10-02, this bullet said the call "never fails with ArityMismatch".)*

- PAT-03 · constitution-summary.md:1922 · Rule (under: PAT-03 — A family has one outer call interface: every clause takes the same number of argu)
  > - **(b) Exact slot count.** A head of arity n matches only a call supplying exactly n argument slots. Each top-level pattern consumes exactly one slot. Surplus arguments are never dropped and missing ones never defaulted, so a wrong argument count selects no clause (NoMatchingBranch). Arity therefore never distinguishes clauses.
  Now:
  > - **(b) Exact slot count.** A head of arity n matches only a call supplying exactly n argument slots. Each top-level pattern consumes exactly one slot. Surplus arguments are never dropped and missing ones never defaulted, so a wrong argument count selects no clause: the call's cardinality is rejected as `ArityMismatch` before any clause is tried or any argument demanded (NEED-05; until Model C, 2026-10-02, it was `NoMatchingBranch`). Arity therefore never distinguishes clauses.

- PAT-11 · constitution-summary.md:2044 · Rule (under: PAT-11 — A clause family is an ordinary callable: it can be passed, called back and dot-ca)
  > - **Zero-argument demand.** A family demanded with zero arguments (bare `Fact` in a value slot, or `Fact()`) is dispatched against the empty supply (CALL-05). No source clause has a zero-arity head, so in every value slot this is NoMatchingBranch.
  Now:
  > - **Zero-argument demand.** A family demanded with zero arguments (bare `Fact` in a value slot) is dispatched against the empty supply (CALL-05). No source clause has a zero-arity head, so in every value slot this is NoMatchingBranch. An explicit call `Fact()` is instead an ordinary call supplying zero slots, which no clause head accepts: the cardinality `ArityMismatch` (NEED-05; until Model C, 2026-10-02, it was NoMatchingBranch too).

- RUN-03 · constitution-summary.md:2407 · Rule (under: RUN-03 — Runtime protection is host policy: it may stop a run, never redefine it)
  > - **Never postponed or absorbed.** No construct can defer, absorb or replace it: not a binding that is never read afterwards, a supplied computation's memo (a reached limit is never a cell's completed outcome, NEED-02), forwarding, a builtin's arity verdict, an earlier ordinary failure, or a consumer's choice. A resource limit is therefore never a slot's recorded outcome (CALL-06). What separates it from an ORDINARY failure: an ordinary failure becomes the completed outcome of the computation that raised it (NEED-02, CALL-06), and a reached limit never does. Both end the run once evaluation that actually occurs raises them, and a supplied computation that is never demanded runs nothing and reaches neither (RUN-08).
  Now:
  > - **Never postponed or absorbed.** No construct can defer, absorb or replace it: not a binding that is never read afterwards, a supplied computation's memo, forwarding, a builtin's arity verdict, an earlier ordinary failure, or a consumer's choice. A demanded cell that reaches a limit stores it as its TERMINAL completion, and the run's budget retains that error, so the cell never restarts and no later semantic work — no further evaluation, memo read, CALLABLE projection, random draw or host operation — runs (NEED-02, NEED-09; C# `NeedCell.Complete` with `EvaluationBudget.RetainTerminal` / `CheckContinuation`). What separates it from an ORDINARY failure: an ordinary failure is the completed outcome of the computation that raised it (NEED-02, CALL-06) and fails only the demands that reach it, while a reached limit is terminal for the whole run; neither is ever a recoverable argument value or a clause mismatch, and neither enters the success-only property cache (NEED-10). *(Phase A3, 2026-10-10: until then this bullet said that "a reached limit is never a cell's completed outcome" and "never a slot's recorded outcome", contradicting `NeedCell.Complete`, NEED-02's "stored terminal completion" and CALL-06 as corrected by the A2 independent review.)* Both end the run once evaluation that actually occurs raises them, and a supplied computation that is never demanded runs nothing and reaches neither (RUN-08).

### PAT-09 — retained prior text (detailed edition; B5-F05)

>   - *(Until Model C: every argument was value-demanded before any clause was tried (PAT-07), a repeated binder had to equal the value bound by its first occurrence (structural value equality), and family binders carried no callable identity.)*
>
> **Why fundamental:** A name means one thing within one binding scope.

Current correction:   - *(Until Model C: every argument was value-demanded before any clause was tried (PAT-07), a repeated binder had to equal the value bound by its first occurrence (structural value equality), and family binders carried no callable identity.)*
- **(c) Forwarded occurrences (decided 2026-09-29; the Q-72 refusal reversed):** *Repeated names constrain independently supplied arguments. When implicit forwarding supplies the same caller binding to several occurrences, each occurrence receives that same complete binding, and no synthetic value/callable merge occurs.* Formula forwarding is by binding name (PAR-07): `D = P + 1` with `P(x, x)` is `D(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, exactly the written `Same(x) = P(x, x) + 1`, so the occurrences agree by construction on a value, and a callable-only or failed argument is its own failure. An explicit call with its own parameters (`Both(a, b) = P(a, b)`) keeps the occurrences independent, as the direct `P(7, 8)` does, and so does the callable alias `Some = P`, whose CALLABLE identity is `P` itself by binding indirection, with no signature of its own (FWD-02, adopted 2026-10-01); bare forwarding `Q(x) = P` follows the formula's by-name rule, `P(x, x)`. (Worked examples: Boundary, Forwarded occurrences.)

**Why fundamental:** A name means one thing within one binding scope.

### RAND-03 — retained prior text (detailed edition; C2-F05)

> - `random(start, end)` / `Math.Random` returns a uniform draw on the exact 10^-34 lattice in `[start, end)`. Both bounds must be finite, `start < end`, and the range must be finite.

Current correction: - `random(start, end)` / `Math.Random` draws a unit fraction `u` uniformly from the lattice `{k·10^-34 | 0 ≤ k < 10^34}` and returns `start + u·(end − start)` in Decimal128 arithmetic; a result that rounds up to `end` folds back to `start`, so every result lies in `[start, end)`. Both bounds must be finite, `start < end`, and the range must be finite. *(Final audit correction, 2026-10-10: formerly "returns a uniform draw on the exact 10^-34 lattice in `[start, end)`"; only the unit fraction lies on that lattice — the scaled result is rounded to Decimal128, so e.g. `random(0, 0.0000000001)` with seed 7 is `0.00000000009108960089237448709689372594955804`, off the lattice — corrected by the sampling contract, `docs/design/seeded-randomness-2026-09.md` §5, and `ScaleRandomUnitFractionToHalfOpenRange`, `Evaluator.Expressions.cs:1110-1117`.)*

### SYN-11 — retained prior text (detailed edition; X7-F03)

**Open owner question (recorded by the final Constitution-wide audit, 2026-10-10; FA-OQ-1, no decision taken here):** the zero-argument VALUE demand of an INLINE alias block — `Inc(x) = x + 1` / `K(z) = count({ Inc })` / `K(1)`, or `Id({ Inc })` with `Id(v) = v` — reports the written-block `UnresolvedImplicitParams` (this rule's Rejection report, by the written shape; C# `EvalInlineAliasValue`, Lean `zeroArgumentDemandError?` `.algorithmExpr` arm), naming the TARGET's written parameter `x` as if it were an implicit parameter of the program, while a NAMED alias `A = Inc` / `count(A)` reports the target's cardinality `ArityMismatch` ("Property 'A' expects 1 parameter…"). FWD-02 makes every callable use of an alias its target's and PAR-05 gives an alias no inferred signature, but no decision record says whether the written-block report (which predates block aliases, 2026-10-01) applies to a block that infers nothing. Both readings reject the program; only the error kind (FORMAL-06) and the wording differ. Options for the owner, without preference here: keep the written-block report and state it (wording fix only), or report the target's cardinality as for a named alias (a paired Lean/C# change). See `open-questions.md` § Final Constitution-wide audit — owner items.

If the name is left to the opens, an open of the nested level is consulted first (RES-02, RES-03). An inline `{ … }` open target and a loaded module are rooted at the prelude and are not nested bodies in this sense (MOD-06, MOD-08).

Replacement:

- A reference written directly in an algorithm's body and one written in a body nested inside it select the same binding when the owner walk selects a declaration and no level between them, the nested body included, declares the name: nesting depth adds no barrier to the walk. If the name is left to the opens, an open of the nested level is consulted first (RES-02, RES-03). An inline `{ … }` open target and a loaded module are rooted at the prelude and are not nested bodies in this sense (MOD-06, MOD-08).

  > - *Callable alias (binding indirection; decided 2026-10-01, superseding the 2026-09-29 wrapper reading).* An OPEN body (no written parameter list, no parameter of its own) whose row resolves to an identity that DECLARES PARAMETERIZED CALLABLE STRUCTURE — a builtin; a clause family, nameable or not; a user algorithm with at least one parameter pattern once its signature is complete (written, inferred, lifted, or itself an alias: chains normalize to one target) — makes `A` a binding of its own whose CALLABLE TARGET is that identity. Every callable use of `A` is the target's: calling `A` with a supply S — directly, by dot-call fallback, as a callback or loop step, or through a parameter that received `A` — is calling the target with S through the target's own invocation (user binder, builtin adapter, clause dispatch, Math or host wrapper), so `A(S)` and `F(S)` have the same accepted and rejected supplies, value, structure, effects and their order, random draws, failures, suspension and cancellation points; `A`'s call-site argument roles, lifting signature, forwarding contract, arity, zero-argument acceptance and callable identity are the target's. No wrapper algorithm and no inherited signature exist. What belongs to the binding stays `A`'s: its declaration and source identity, its exposure (it reads the target), its zero-argument property cache entry (`A` read bare is the target's zero-supply demand, evaluated once per run for `A`; `A()` is fresh), and the declarations its own body writes — never its target's members, so member access written on `A` selects its own declared member or takes the ordinary extension fallback, and `open A` is rejected like any callable that needs a call (a callable that flows out through `A` — a parameter, a callback — is the target itself and navigates the target's members). The target is fixed by resolution in `A`'s own scope, never re-resolved at a use site; a host-built alias cycle is rejected. When the resolved identity declares no parameters, the row is an ordinary zero-parameter property that reads it (the target's cache entry), never an alias. *History:* from 2026-09-29 to this decision the exact alias was a WRAPPER — an open body took F's parameter patterns VERBATIM as its signature and called F with them rebuilt from its own bindings, its inherited names encapsulated (RES-05) — which is exact only for an identity whose acceptance is the ordinary binder (the callable-capability rule's exact-alias contract); the alias-indirection investigation (`alias-indirection/final-report.md`) found the wrapper unnecessary: binding indirection reproduces every user alias the wrapper did and also aliases builtins and families exactly.

  > > **Current Q-33 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-09 (committed as `d7dae7d8`; original implementation over `main` @ `4d7cac19`):** the owner decided Q-33 — P0: the current parse is law; no new diagnostic — the recommendation of `../q33-parser-boundary-investigation/final-report.md`. *The law (SYN-11):* a line-final star is no exception: a `*` at the end of a physical line is classified by SYN-11 exactly like any other `*`; if the next significant token, including across blank lines or comments, can begin an operand and does not begin a declaration, the star is binary multiplication, and expression parsing then continues across the newline under SYN-08 with ordinary precedence unchanged (`X = A*` newline `X` is `X = A * X`, which leaves no output row; `x, y = V*` newline `x + y` is `(V * x) + y`, never `V * (x + y)`); the layout alone introduces no warning or error. A spread row that another row follows ends with `A*,`; a definition body ending in a spread is closed as `X = (A*)` or `X = { A* }`; a following declaration head also ends the expression. Rejected: a warning (P1, P1ANY), a new error (P2A, P2B), and newline rules that would silently change accepted values (P4A, P4B). *Implementation:* no production parser, evaluator, diagnostic, grammar, AST, Lean-semantics or public-API change — documentation (AGENTS.md, `syntax.md`, `KatLang.ebnf`, `tutorial.md`, `SEMANTIC-ALIGNMENT.md`), the new `LineFinalStarLawTests`, the repaired `ModuleCoordinateSpaceTests` spread fixture, and the regenerated spec case `line-final-star-in-definition-continues`. **Q-33 RESOLVED BY DECISION; § Decide before release now holds no open question** (the other open questions stay open). ## Q-25 — owner decision and implementation — 2026-10-10

### HO-03 (with HO-02, HO-04, HO-05, VAL-04, VAL-06, VAL-08, SEQ-04, COLL-04, PAT-11, LOOP-07, FORMAL-05)

1. **2026-04-08 · #37 (a66564b / 83eccae):** `map`/`filter`/`reduce` introduced; "transform/step must return exactly one value" — a callback's EMITTED values were counted, so a two-row body was rejected.
2. **2026-06 · #132 (9a4c70f):** property, call and builtin results became one-value boundaries; the callback check was kept, its rejection described as "an error, not a silently-grouped value".
3. **2026-07 · #135 (0ca55e9):** collection builtins return exact lists; the issue asked to preserve the existing callback-result contract and not to capture multiple callback outputs silently for `map`, and AGENTS listed "the strict single-value `map`/`reduce` callback contract" among the deliberate non-value-boundaries.
4. **2026-09/10 · constitution audit:** recorded as HO-03 with a known tension (η-expansion changes results; `map(xs, Id)` is not the identity with `()`), the ALGHO open question, PV-32 and PV-33 (intentional exceptions), X-32 and Q-25 (options (a) keep, (b) re-count at the call boundary); moved to § Can wait on 2026-10-03.
5. **2026-10-09 · D1:** a clause-family callback had been accepted through the family driver's call-boundary re-count while the same clause written as a user algorithm was rejected; D1 made the family obey the raw-count contract too (`recount: false` for both).
6. **2026-10-10 · focused investigation:** policies A (strict), B (ordinary call result) and C (call result, `()` rejected) compared on 92 frozen programs with Lean and C# prototypes; verdict DECISION READY, recommendation B (`../q25-callback-result-investigation/final-report.md`).
7. **2026-10-10 · owner decision: Option B.** *a `map` transform or `reduce` step returns the ordinary result of calling its callback.* Implemented in Lean and C# together; evidence `../q25-callback-result-investigation/implementation/`.

**Why the history is superseded.** After ordinary calls became value boundaries, retaining the raw-output callback restriction broke compositionality, identity mapping and wrapper equivalence: `[1].map(D)` with `D(x) = x, x` failed while `[1].map(G)` with `G(x) = D(x)` and `[1].map(H)` with `H(x) = (x, x)` gave the same value `[(1, 1)]`, `map([(), 1], Id)` failed on its own element, and no reduce step could return `()`.

**The superseded texts (kept as history, not law).** The complete former HO-03 of the detailed edition:

> ### HO-03 — Callback results have their own contract: `map`/`reduce` need exactly one emitted non-`()` value; `filter` needs a Boolean
>
> **Class:** BOUNDARY RULE, EVALUATION RULE
> **Status:** Current — see open question
> **Rule:**
> - **`map` and `reduce`.** A `map` transform and a `reduce` step must each EMIT exactly one top-level value that is not `()`. A list, including `[]`, is one value. The callback's own output is judged by its emitted count and is not re-counted at the call's value boundary.
>   - A body with several rows is `ArityMismatch` "map transform must return a single element" or "reduce step must return a single accumulator value".
>   - So is a body that yields `()`.
>   - A multi-valued result produced through an inner call is accepted, because the inner call is a value boundary.
> - **`filter`.** A `filter` predicate result must be a Boolean (see BOOL: only Booleans have a truth value).
>
> **Why fundamental:** It decides which callbacks are legal and what `map` can produce. For example, `map` can never produce a `()` element. It is also the one place where a callee's written row count is observable despite the call-result value boundary (see VAL).
>
> **Normal example:**
> - `h03a.kat`: `D(x) = x, x ⏎ G(x) = D(x) ⏎ H(x) = (x, x) ⏎ [D(1)], map([1], G), map([1], H)` → `ok S[L[S[1, 1]], L[S[1, 1]], L[S[1, 1]]]`.
> - `h03b.kat`: `map([1], D)` → `err ArityMismatch` "map transform must return a single element: Bad arity".
> - `h03c.kat` / `h03d.kat`: `Id(x) = x`. `[Id(()), Id(1)]` → `ok L[S[], 1]`, while `map([(), 1], Id)` → `err ArityMismatch` (same message).
> - `h03e.kat`: `L0(x) = [] ⏎ map([1, 2], L0)` → `ok L[L[], L[]]`.
> - `h03g.kat`: `R(x, acc) = x, acc ⏎ reduce([1, 2], R, 0)` → `err ArityMismatch` "reduce step must return a single accumulator value".
> - `h03f.kat`: `filter([1, 2], {x})` → `err TypeMismatch` "filter predicate result must be a Boolean value (true or false), but was numeric value 1".
>
> **Boundary / caveat:**
> - The contract judges only the result. Binding is HO-02.
> - `while`/`repeat` step outputs are the multi-slot state protocol, not this contract (see LOOP).
> - A callback body whose row is a completed multi-slot loop returns ONE value since Q-26 (2026-10-04), exactly like a helper returning it: `Fib(x, y) = y, x + y` / `[0, 1].map({ repeat(Fib, 2, x, 1) })` and `map([0, 1], H)` with `H(x) = repeat(Fib, 2, x, 1)` both give `L[S[1, 2], S[2, 3]]`. *(Formerly the loop's slot count leaked into this contract and the block form was rejected.)* The contract itself is unchanged: `{ repeat(Fib, 2, x, 1)* }` is still several outputs.
> - `reduce`'s `initial` is a value slot (HO-04). With an empty collection it is returned as the result: `reduce([], Sub, 7)` → `7`.
>
> **Known tension:**
> - η-expansion changes the outcome: `map([1], D)` fails while `map([1], G)` with `G(x) = D(x)` succeeds.
> - `map(xs, Id)` is not the identity when `xs` contains `()`.
>
> This is in tension with "callback ≡ ordinary call" and "values stay values" (w1-suspicions [L2], [L3], [C3], [C4], all classified "intentional exception").
>
> **Evidence:**
> - Issues: #37 ("transform/step must return exactly one value"), #41 (PARTIALLY CURRENT: predicate result shape), #165 (predicate must be Boolean)
> - C# (D1 reconciliation, 2026-10-09): `Evaluator.Results.cs` `ExpectSingleEmittedValue` / `ExpectSingleAccumulator` / `ExpectSingleMappedElement`; sync and async callback dispatch reach `Evaluator.Needs.cs` `EvalNeedCallbackBody`, which passes `recount: false` to `EvalNeedFamilySupply` and `EvalNeedUserSupply`. Ordinary family calls pass `true`; loop steps read the selected body's row supply through `InvokeLoopStepSupply`.
> - Lean (D1 reconciliation, 2026-10-09): `lean/KatLang.lean` `expectSingleValueWith`, `expectSingleAccumulator` / `expectSingleMappedElement`; `evalUserCallbackCallCounted` and `evalConditionalCallbackCallCounted` both preserve the callback's own emitted count (`recount = false`). The production model did not change in D1.
> - Tests:
>   - Lean `CoreTests/SequenceCallbackBuiltins.lean` `test83`/`test84*` (`:640-707`), `test91` (`:911`, the empty-result map);
>   - `EvaluatorSequenceCallbackTests.Eval_Map_MultiOutputTransformResult_FailsWithContext` (`:433`), `.Eval_Map_EmptyTransformResult_FailsWithContext` (`:404`);

The complete former HO-03 of the rules-only edition:

> ### HO-03 — Callback results have their own contract: `map`/`reduce` need exactly one emitted non-`()` value; `filter` needs a Boolean
>
> **Class:** BOUNDARY RULE, EVALUATION RULE · **Status:** Current — see open question
>
> **Rule:**
> - **`map` and `reduce`.** A `map` transform and a `reduce` step must each EMIT exactly one top-level value that is not `()`. A list, including `[]`, is one value. The callback's own output is judged by its emitted count and is not re-counted at the call's value boundary.
>   - A body with several rows is `ArityMismatch` "map transform must return a single element" or "reduce step must return a single accumulator value".
>   - So is a body that yields `()`.
>   - A multi-valued result produced through an inner call is accepted, because the inner call is a value boundary.
> - **`filter`.** A `filter` predicate result must be a Boolean (see BOOL: only Booleans have a truth value).

The register's open question is preserved verbatim under its § Already resolved record in `open-questions.md`; every other replaced line of the detailed and rules-only editions, the register and the issue ledger is quoted below.

**Surviving semantics.** A `map` transform or `reduce` step returns the ordinary call result of its callback: the ONE value the call boundary delivers — several rows one sequence value, `()` and `[]` ordinary values; `map` stores it as one element, `reduce` passes it as one accumulator, and nothing is spread; no cardinality or non-empty check. Errors propagate as in the ordinary call, `MissingOutput` included. `filter` keeps its Boolean contract; loop steps keep their row semantics (LOOP-03); Model-C demand, clause-family selection, patterns, error categories, evaluation order and budgets are unchanged; D1's agreement of family and user callbacks survives.

**Must NOT appear as current law:** "a `map` transform must return a single element"; "a `reduce` step must return a single accumulator value"; "a callback must emit exactly one value"; "a callback may not return `()`"; "a callback result is not a value boundary"; "the callback's raw emitted count is judged"; "a mapper returning `()` skips the element"; "Q-25 remains open".

**Every replaced or removed record line, verbatim (mechanically extracted from the pre-decision snapshot; Q-25, 2026-10-10).** Each quoted line is the complete pre-decision line; its replacement is in the current record, and a removed line was moved (the Q-25 register record, now under its historical heading) or merged.

- Detailed edition, pre-decision line 7958 (replaced):

  > **Boundary / caveat:** Plain binding and forwarding demand nothing (NEED-01, NEED-08), so an invoking slot never causes an earlier VALUE read of its callable. An explicit `f()` through a forwarded parameter is fresh: `Call0(f) = f() ⏎ Call0(A), Call0(A), A` with `A = tick()` → `S[1, 2, 3]` after three ticks (`h04c`, re-run 2026-10-09, Phase A2, six routes). *(Until Model C: "Ordinary eager parameter binding may already have evaluated a zero-argument-acceptable callable once, to establish its value channel (HO-01)", and h04c gave `2, 3, 1`.)* Projection happens at the first invocation, after the collection is demanded: `Through(xs, f) = map(xs, f)` / `Through([], tick())` is `L[]` with no host event, `Through([1], tick())` is `NotAnAlgorithm` with no host event (the projection never demands the tick), and `map([trace(1), 2], 5)` is `NotAnAlgorithm` after `[trace(1)]`; `map([], 5)`, `filter([], 5)` and `reduce([], 5, 7)` give `L[]`, `L[]` and `7`, while `reduce([1], 5, 7)` and `filter([1], 1 / 0)` are `NotAnAlgorithm`. A forwarded clause family keeps its callback cardinality (D1): `F(0) = 10` / `F(n) = n` / `Fwd(f, xs) = map(xs, f)` / `Fwd(F, [0, 5])` is `L[10, 5]`.
